BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r3.claim: Being on a journey means traveling toward and turning to one’s destination; lacking a scribe includes lack of writing skill or writing materials, and the verse does not mention witnesses because their availability follows the same rationale.

BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r4.claim: A pledge is collateral that must be delivered to the lender; an undelivered pledge does not compel the pledgor to hand it over. Travel is mentioned because writing and witnesses are often unavailable, not because pledges are restricted to travel.

BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r5.claim: The Prophet pawned his armor to a Jew in Medina for twenty measures of barley for his family.
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r5.anchor: وقد رهن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم درعه في المدينة من يهودي بعشرين صاعا من شعير

BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r6.claim: When the lender trusts the debtor and waives collateral, the debtor must repay the entrusted debt without delay; the debt is called a trust because it rests on his liability.
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r6.anchor: وهو المديون والائتمان الوثوق بأمانة الرجل

BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r7.claim: Witnesses must not conceal testimony when summoned; anyone concealing it commits a sin of the heart.
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r7.anchor: أيها الشهود إذا دعيتم إلى الحاكم لأدائها على وجهها

BURSEVI:v1p362/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p362/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p362/r1.claim: The sin is assigned to the heart because concealment begins by inwardly suppressing testimony; attributing an act to its working organ makes the charge more emphatic.
BURSEVI:v1p362/r1.anchor: كتمان الشهادة هو أن يضمرها ولا يتكلم بها فلما كان الإثم مقترفا بالقلب أسند إليه

BURSEVI:v1p362/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p362/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p362/r2.claim: The heart is the root and noblest seat of the self: its soundness or corruption governs the whole body, so the sin is not merely of the tongue, which only expresses it.
BURSEVI:v1p362/r2.anchor: ولأن القلب هو رأس الأعراض والمضغة التي إن صلحت صلح الجسد كله وإن فسدت فسد الجسد كله

BURSEVI:v1p362/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p362/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p362/r3.claim: Heart-actions are roots from which bodily deeds branch; faith and unbelief are the roots of good and evil, so concealment of testimony is a grave heart-sin.
BURSEVI:v1p362/r3.anchor: ولأن أفعال القلوب أعظم من أفعال سائر الجوارح وهي لها كالأصول التي تتشعب منها

BURSEVI:v1p362/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p362/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v1p362/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās counts associating partners with God, false testimony, and concealing testimony among the greatest grave sins.
BURSEVI:v1p362/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أكبر الكبائر الإشراك بالله لقوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p362/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p362/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p362/r5.claim: God knows deeds and will repay good with good and evil with evil; false testimony and concealed testimony lead to Hell and reveal corruption of the heart, aided by common motives such as enmity.
BURSEVI:v1p362/r5.anchor: فيجازيكم به إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر

BURSEVI:v1p362/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p362/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p362/r6.claim: Religious people are either stationary, confined to outward form with no access to inner meaning, or traveling from bodily form toward spiritual meaning; the stationary resemble a chick trapped in its shell and have scribes recording outward deeds.
BURSEVI:v1p362/r6.anchor: واعلم أن أهل الدين طائفتان الواقفون

BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r1.claim: A traveler moves from outward form and bodily confinement into inward meaning and the spacious realm of spirits; travelers are either walkers or flyers.
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r1.anchor: والسائر من لم يقم ولم ينزل في منزل فهو مسافر من عالم الصورة إلى عالم المعنى

BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r2.claim: The walker follows the path of the religious law and reason; the flyer moves on the wings of love and aspiration toward ultimate reality, while remaining tethered to the law.
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r2.anchor: فالسيار من يسير بقدم الشرع والعقل على جادة الطريقة

BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r3.claim: In the inward reading, the traveling walker is freed from bodily confinement, senses, and scribal surveillance; some mystics say the left recorder wrote nothing for twenty years, or that the right recorder asked to record heart-deeds and was told the obligations sufficed.
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r3.anchor: إلى السيار الذي تخلص من سجن الجسد وقيد الحواس

BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r4.claim: The pledge is the walker’s heart, kept for God alone and held between the fingers of the All-Merciful.
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r4.anchor: إشارة إلى اليسار الذي له قلب فيرهنه عند الله تعالى فالرهان هي القلوب التي ليس فيها غير الله

BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r5.claim: The flying lover has lost heart and reason and is carried by divine attraction, so no pledge is demanded of him; he is overcome by God’s force, and only the destitute lover can bear the trust.
BURSEVI:v1p362#2/r5.anchor: فأما الطيار الذي هو عاشق مفقود القلب مسلوب العقل مجذوب السير فلا يطالب بالرهن

AKHFASH:v1p206/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p206/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p206/r1.claim: رهان is a regular plural of رهن, like حبال from حبل.
AKHFASH:v1p206/r1.anchor: قال {فرهان مقبوضة} تقول: "رهن"، و"رهان" مثل: "حبل" و"حبال".

AKHFASH:v1p206/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p206/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
AKHFASH:v1p206/r2.claim: Abu Amr gives the form رهن, but al-Akhfash calls it awkward because فعلا rarely has the plural pattern فعل.
AKHFASH:v1p206/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: "فرهن" وهي قبيحة لأن "فعلا" لا يجمع على "فعل" إلا قليلا شاذا

AKHFASH:v1p206/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p206/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p206/r3.claim: Rare examples of that plural pattern include سقف, قلب, and لحد; Qur'an 43:33 also has سقفا من فضة.
AKHFASH:v1p206/r3.anchor: زعم أنهم يقولون: "سقف" و"سقف" وقرأوا هذه الآية {سقفا من فضة} وقالوا: "قلب" و"قلب" و"قلب" من "قلب النخلة" و"لحد" و"لحد" ل"لحد القبر" وهذا شاذ

AKHFASH:v1p206/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p206/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p206/r4.claim: Other unusual faʿl plurals are attested, but رهان remains preferable to relying on such exceptional forms.
AKHFASH:v1p206/r4.anchor: وقد جمعوا "فعلا" على "فعل" فقالوا: "ثط" و"ثط"، و"جون" و"جون"، و"ورد" و"ورد". وقد يكون "رهن" جماعة ل"الرهان" كأنه جمع الجماعة و"رهان" أمثل* من هذا الاضطرار.

AKHFASH:v1p206/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p206/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
AKHFASH:v1p206/r5.claim: Abu Amr says Arabs use رهن to distinguish it from رهان for racehorses.
AKHFASH:v1p206/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: "قالت العرب: "رهن" ليفصلوا بينه وبين رهان الخيل

AKHFASH:v1p206/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p206/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p206/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash generalizes that a collective expressed on the pattern فعل can also be said as فعل.
AKHFASH:v1p206/r6.anchor: قال الاخفش: "كل جماعة على "فعل" فإنه يقال فيها "فعل".

AKHFASH:v1p206/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p206/r7.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p206/r7.claim: سهام خشن shows that the adjective can take a lightened plural form.
AKHFASH:v1p206/r7.anchor: وقد قالوا: "سهم خشن" في "سهام خشن". خفيفة.

AKHFASH:v1p206/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p206/r8.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p206/r8.claim: فليؤد derives from أدى يؤدّي, which explains its hamza; اؤتمن likewise has root hamza from أمانة.
AKHFASH:v1p206/r8.anchor: وقال {فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته} وهي من "أدى" "يؤدي" فلذلك همز و"اؤتمن" همزها لانها من

AKHFASH:v1p206/r9.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p206/r9.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p206/r9.claim: At a fresh start the connecting alif remains, so the root hamza is not separately pronounced and two hamzas do not meet.
AKHFASH:v1p206/r9.anchor: "الأمانة" [و] موضع الفاء منها همزة، إلا أنك إذا استأنفت ثبتت الف الوصل فيها فلم تهمز موضع الفاء لئلا تجتمع همزتان.

FARRA:v1p187/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p187/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p187/r1.claim: In تكون ميتة, feminine agreement follows the semantic noun; in إن تك مثقال حبة, the verb likewise follows the understood حبة despite masculine مثقال.

FARRA:v1p187/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p187/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p187/r2.claim: Poetry also lets a feminine verb agree with an implied feminine referent such as hand, death, or the plural hooked sticks.
FARRA:v1p187/r2.anchor: فأنث فعل الداعي وهو ذكر لأنه ذهب إلى الموتة

FARRA:v1p187/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p187/r4.speaker: مجاهد
FARRA:v1p187/r4.claim: Mujāhid reads فرهن as the plural of رهان, just as ثمر can mean fruits.
FARRA:v1p187/r4.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد فرهن على جمع الرهان كما قال كلوا من ثمره

FARRA:v1p187/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p187/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p187/r5.claim: Some grammarians allow قلبه in the accusative, by analogy with “you made your judgment foolish” and “you sinned your heart.”
FARRA:v1p187/r5.anchor: فإن يكن حقا فهو من جهة قولك

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p100/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p100/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p100/r1.claim: رهن is the plural of رهان; the reading رهان is therefore a plural formed from an already plural form.

MAJAZ:v1p83/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p83/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
MAJAZ:v1p83/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr says رهان is used for horse-race stakes and cites a poem about pledging them.
MAJAZ:v1p83/r5.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: الرهان في الخيل، وأنشد

MAJAZ:v1p83/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p83/r6.speaker: قعنب بن أم صاحب
MAJAZ:v1p83/r6.claim: Qanʿab's poem uses رهن for a stake or wager.
MAJAZ:v1p83/r6.anchor: وأنشد قول قعنب بن أم صاحب من بني عبد الله بن غطفان: بانت سعاد

NAHHAS:v1p348/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك وأبو العالية
NAHHAS:v1p348/r2.claim: These authorities read ولم تجدوا كتابا; another transmission from Ibn Abbas gives the same reading.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك وأبو العالية ( ولم تجدوا كتابا

NAHHAS:v1p348/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p348/r3.claim: Al-Nahhas calls كتابا an anomalous reading; the common reading is supported by the prior command وليكتب بينكم كاتب.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r3.anchor: قال أبو جعفر هذه القراءة شاذة والعامة على خلافها وقل ما يخرج شيء عن قراءة العامة

NAHHAS:v1p348/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p348/r4.claim: كتاب can denote a collective group of writers.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r4.anchor: نسق الكلام يدل على كاتب قال تعالى قبل هذا وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل وكتاب يقضي جماعة

NAHHAS:v1p348/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وأهل الكوفة وأهل المدينة
NAHHAS:v1p348/r5.claim: Ali, the Kufans, and the Medinans read فرهان with fatḥa on rāʾ and a long vowel.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r5.anchor: هذه قراءة علي بن أبي طالب

NAHHAS:v1p348/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v1p348/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reads رهن with two dammas, which is also Abu Amr’s reading.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( فرهن ) بضمتين وهي قراءة أبي عمرو

NAHHAS:v1p348/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r7.speaker: عاصم بن أبي النجود
NAHHAS:v1p348/r7.claim: Asim ibn Abi al-Najud reads رهن with a still hāʾ; the reading is also transmitted from Meccans.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r7.anchor: وقرأ عاصم بن أبي النجود ( فرهن ) بإسكان الهاء وتروى عن أهل مكة

NAHHAS:v1p348/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p348/r8.claim: The regular plural is رهان, like بغل وبغال and كبش وكباش; رهن may follow the كتاب/كتب pattern, while the سقف/سقف analysis is less apt.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r8.anchor: الباب في هذا رهان كما تقول بغل وبغال وكبش وكباش و رهن سبيله أن يكون جمع رهان مثل كتاب وكتب

NAHHAS:v1p348/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p348/r9.claim: In رهن with sukūn, damma may have been dropped for heaviness; another analysis treats it as a plural adjective like سهام حشر, which he favors over a non-adjective analogy.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r9.anchor: رهن بإسكان الهاء سبيله أن تكون الضمة حذفت منه لثقلها

NAHHAS:v1p348/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p348/r10.claim: فليؤد derives from hamzated أداء; a softened hamza may become wāw, but not alif or an intermediate vowel after kasra.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r10.anchor: فليؤد ) من الأداء مهموز ويجوز تخفيف همزة فتقلب الهمزة واوا ولا تقلب ألفا

NAHHAS:v1p348/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p348/r11.claim: The origin of اؤتمن is أأتمن from أمانة; simplifying the two hamzas and adjacent sukūns explains deletion of the yāʾ in الذي تمن.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r11.anchor: الذي اؤتمن ) مهموز في الأصل لأنه من الأمانة ففاء الفعل همزة والأصل في اؤتمن أأتمن

NAHHAS:v1p348/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r12.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
NAHHAS:v1p348/r12.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman reads ولا يكتموا الشهادة as a prohibition addressed to absent people.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r12.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن ( ولا يكتموا الشهادة ) جعله نهيا لغيب

NAHHAS:v1p348/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p348/r13.claim: آثم قلبه permits several parses: āthim as predicate with قلب as its subject, āthim as a subject with qalb as its subject, delayed predicate, or apposition.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r13.anchor: فيه وجوه إن شئت رفعت آثما على أنه خبر إن وقلبه فاعل سد مسد الخبر

NAHHAS:v1p348/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r14.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v1p348/r14.claim: Abu Hatim permits آثم قلبه as an intensive construction, comparing أنت عربي قلبا.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r14.anchor: وأجاز أبو حاتم فإنه آثم قلبه قال كما تقول هو آثم قلب الإثم

NAHHAS:v1p348/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p348/r15.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects Abu Hatim’s analysis because قلبه is definite; one cannot say أنت عربي قلبه.
NAHHAS:v1p348/r15.anchor: وقد خطىء أبو حاتم في هذا لأن قلبه معرفة ولا يجوز ما قال في المعرفة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r1.claim: In one reading attributed to Ubayy, lacking a scribe entails lacking a pen, inkpot, and paper as well; the wording gathers these writing materials together.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : ان لم تجدوا كاتبا ، ولم تجدوا قلما ، ولا دواة ، قال : وذكر الصحيفة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r2.claim: Although scribes are plentiful, the verse can refer to lacking ink and parchment.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r2.anchor: حدثني عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس : الكتاب كثير ، ولكنه يعني : دواة وقرطاسا .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r3.claim: The travel condition means being unable to write the debt while traveling.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : وان كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا يعني : لم تقدروا على كتابة الدين في السفر

IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas read “a document” rather than “a scribe,” explaining that travelers may find a book but lack ink and paper; Mujahid and Abu al-ʿAliya report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، انه كان يقرا ولم تجدوا كتابا قال : ربما وجدوا كتابا ، ولم يجدوا الدواة والصحفية

IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r5.claim: A pledge must be physically received by the creditor to count as a pledge.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قوله : فرهان مقبوضة قال : لا يكون الرهن الا مقبوضة يقبضه الذي له المال

IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r6.claim: The creditor should take the pledge from the debtor.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : فرهان مقبوضة يقول : فليرتهن الذي له الحق من المطلوب

IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r7.claim: A pledge is only taken while traveling.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد فرهان مقبوضة قال : لا يكون الرهن الا في السفر

IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r8.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r8.claim: If writing is available during a journey, the creditor should record the deferred debt instead of taking collateral.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p568/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك فرهن مقبوضة يعني بذلك : انه لا يصلح اذا كان بيعا في سفر ، اذا وجد كتابا ، ان ياخذ رهنا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r1.speaker: عامر
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r1.claim: The collateral clause is abrogated by the later trust clause.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r1.anchor: عن عامر ، في قوله : فرهان مقبوضة قال هي منسوخة فان امن بعضكم بعضا يعني : نسخه ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r2.claim: Abu Saʿid says the trust clause abrogated what came before it.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري ، انه تلا هذه الاية : يايها الذين امنوا اذا تداينتم بدين حتى بلغ فان امن بعضكم بعضا قال : هذه نسخت ما قبلها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r3.speaker: الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r3.claim: When the creditor trusts the debtor, it is permissible not to write or obtain witnesses.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي ، في قوله : فان امن بعضكم بعضا قال : لا باس اذا امنته ، الا تكتب ولا تشهد

IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r4.claim: When no scribe is available, writing and witnessing are obligatory; a pledge is not an option when a scribe is available, just as a prescribed alternative applies only when its condition is met.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك فان امن بعضكم بعضا فمن لم يجد ، فانها عزمة ان يكتب ويشهد ، ولا ياخذ رهنا اذا وجد كاتبا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r5.claim: If the debtor is trustworthy to the creditor, the creditor need not take collateral because of that trust.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : فان امن بعضكم بعضا يقول : فان كان الذي عليه الحق امينا عند صاحب الحق ، فلم يرتهن ، لثقته

IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r6.speaker: حماد بن أبي سليمان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r6.claim: The trust clause points to good character and the ethical conduct God taught them.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r6.anchor: عن حماد بن أبي سليمان ، في قوله : فان امن بعضكم بعضا قال : اخلاق ، دلهم عليها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r7.speaker: الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r7.claim: Once the debtor is entrusted, the matter becomes one of returning the trust.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p570/r7.anchor: عن الشعبي ، في قوله : فليؤد الذي اؤتمن امانته قال : صار الامر إلى الامانة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r1.claim: The debtor must repay the right owed to its owner.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : فليؤد الذي اؤتمن امانته يقول : ليؤد الحق الذي عليه إلى صاحبه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r2.claim: The debtor is warned to fear God.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، قال : خوف الله ، الذي عليه الحق ، فقال : وليتق الله ربه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r3.claim: Do not conceal testimony in court; when called, present the testimony accurately as it stands.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : ولا تكتموا الشهادة يعني : عند الحكام ، يقول : من اشهد على حق ، فليقمها على جهها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r4.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r4.claim: No one may conceal testimony, even when it is against oneself, one’s parents, or close relatives.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r4.anchor: عن الربيع ولا تكتموا الشهادة فلا يحل لاحد ان يكتم شهادة هي عنده ، وان كانت على نفسه أو الوالدين أو الاقربين

IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r5.claim: Concealing testimony is a major sin.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قال : ومن الكبائر ، كتمان الشهادة ، لان الله يقول : ومن يكتمها فانه اثم قلبه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r6.claim: The sinful heart is the heart of one who conceals testimony by failing to testify when called.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : ومن يكتمها يعني الشهادة ، لا يشهد بها اذا دعى لها فانه اثم قلبه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r7.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r7.claim: A sinful heart is a corrupt heart.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r7.anchor: عن السدى ، قوله : فانه اثم قلبه يقول : فاجر قلبه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r8.claim: God knows whether people conceal testimony or establish it.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p571/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : والله بما تعملون عليم يعني : من كتمان الشهادة ، واقامتها عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r3.claim: The next verse gives pledge as the alternative when a writer cannot be found, without making unwritten testimony an intermediate option; thus a writer may also be one of the witnesses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r3.anchor: فلم يجعل بين فقدان الكاتب وبين الرهن درجة وهي الشهادة بلا كتابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r1.claim: Writing and testimony rules apply in ordinary settled conditions when available; when travel prevents finding someone to write or witness, a pledge supplies the final transactional arrangement, extended to similar circumstances.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r1.anchor: فجميع ما تقدم حكم في الحضر والمكنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r2.claim: Rihān is a plural of rahn, also pluralized as ruhan; the majority of the ten readers vocalize it with kasra then fatḥa, while Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr use ḍamma on both letters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r2.anchor: والرهان جمع رهن ويجمع أيضا على رهن بضم الراء وضم الهاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r3.claim: Rahn names the pledged object by its verbal noun; the debtor places property in the creditor’s possession as security, and the root means detention, as in the verse about every soul held by its deeds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r3.anchor: والرهن هنا اسم للشيء المرهون تسمية للمفعول بالمصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r4.claim: Zuhayr’s line uses a pledge that cannot be released as an image of a debt secured by property held until payment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r4.anchor: قال زهير : وفارقتك برهن لا فكاك له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r5.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs commonly pledged property for guarantees and blood-money, sometimes even sons or prominent men as hostages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r5.anchor: فقد كانوا يرهنون في الحمالات والديات إلى أن يقع دفعها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r6.speaker: الأعشى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r6.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s poem recalls Kisrā seeking children as hostages, which the speaker vowed not to provide lest they be corrupted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r6.anchor: قال الأعشى يذكر أن كسرى رام أخذ رهائن من أبنائهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن همام السلولي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r7.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hammām al-Sulūlī’s verse describes escaping danger while leaving Mālik as a hostage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r7.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن همام السلولي : فلما خشيت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r8.speaker: كعب بن الأشرف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r8.claim: Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf to pledge his sons as hostages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p120/r8.anchor: ومن حديث كعب بن الأشرفف أنه قال لعبد الرحمن بن عوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r1.claim: If the parties trust one another, the creditor is the one trusting and the debtor is the one trusted with the creditor’s property or right.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r1.anchor: أي إن أمن كل من المتداينين الآخر أي وثق بعضكم بأمانة بعض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r2.claim: Amāna derives from giving security; it can name the trusted property itself, and its possessive construction resembles a verbal noun joined to its object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r2.anchor: والأمانة مصدر آمنه إذا جعله آمنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r3.claim: Calling a debt or pledge an amāna gives the right gravity: failing to return it is betrayal, and a Prophetic report commands returning deposits without reciprocating betrayal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث : أد الأمانة إلى من ائتمنك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r4.claim: The Prophet commands returning a trust to its owner and not betraying someone even if that person betrayed you.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r4.anchor: أد الأمانة إلى من ائتمنك ولا تخن من خانك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r5.claim: Performance means payment or fulfillment, return of the thing itself or its equivalent when fungible, and not denying the debt, as in the command to return trusts to their owners.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r5.anchor: ورد الشيء أو رد مثله فيما لا تقصد أعيانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r6.claim: For the majority who treat debt documentation as recommended, this trust provision completes the guidance: parties may document and witness, or rely on their known honesty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p122/r6.anchor: تعتبر تكميلا لطلب الكتابة والإشهاد طلب ندب واستحباب عند الذين حملوا الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r1.claim: The trust clause is followed by a charge to both parties to fulfill what they owe and fear God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r1.anchor: وأتبع هذا البيان بوصاية كلا المتعاملين بأن يؤديا الأمانة ويتقيا الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r2.speaker: الشعبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī, Ibn Jurayj, Jābir ibn Zayd, al-Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān, and an attribution to Abū Saʿīd say mutual trust abrogated the earlier duty to write and witness debts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r2.anchor: وهو قول الشعبي ، وابن جريج ، وجابر بن زيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r3.claim: If Abū Saʿīd’s position is sound, the author says their term abrogation uses an older sense meaning specification of general circumstances or times.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r3.anchor: ومحمل قولهم وقولل أبي سعيد إن صح ذلك عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r4.speaker: الطبري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r4.claim: Those who retain obligatory writing and testimony, including al-Ṭabarī, confine the trust clause to the travel-pledge case; the author says al-Ṭabarī’s explanation is unclear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r4.anchor: كما صرح به الطبري ولم يأت بكلام واضح في ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r5.claim: The author suggests this narrow view could mean that travelers lacking a pledge may proceed only if they trust each other, though its adherents do not clearly state this and may omit it to encourage mutual generosity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r5.anchor: إن هذه الآية تعني حالة تعذر وجود الرهن في حالة السفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r6.claim: The author prefers an independent rule covering every debt setting and transaction: testimony, pledge, repayment, and sale; the undefined baʿḍ includes trust from either direction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r6.anchor: أن هذه الآية تشريع مستقل يعم جميع الأحوال المتعلقة بالديون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r7.claim: A creditor trusts a debtor by dispensing with witnesses and a pledge; a debtor trusts a creditor by giving a pledge worth more than the debt, so each must honor the other’s entrusted right.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r7.anchor: فرب الدين يأتمن المدين إذا لم ير حاجة إلى الإشهاد عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p123/r8.claim: The debtor must repay without delay or denial; the creditor holding an overvalued pledge must return it without denial or withholding any part, since the collateral exceeds the debt.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r1.claim: Amāna refers both to the quality of being trustworthy and to the entrusted object.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r2.claim: The author rejects pre-Islamic foreclosure, by which the creditor became owner of a pledge after nonpayment at the deadline; the Prophet forbade a pledge from being closed off in this way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r2.anchor: فيؤخذ من هذا التفسير إبطال غلق الرهن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r3.claim: The Prophet says that a pledge is not forfeited to the creditor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r3.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( لا يغلق الرهن )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r4.claim: Zuhayr’s verse reflects the old practice of a pledge becoming locked and irredeemable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r4.anchor: قال زهير : وفارقتك برهنن لا فكاك له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r5.claim: Mutual trust means both parties say they need no witnesses because each trusts the other; this avoids reviving suspicion between debtors and creditors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r5.anchor: أن يقول كلا المتعاملين للآخر : لا حاجة لنا بالإشهاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r6.claim: Repeating God’s name before the command to fear Him adds solemn awe even though a pronoun could have been used.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p124/r6.anchor: وذكر اسم الجلالة فيه مع إمكان الاستغناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r1.claim: The majority retain the hamza in alladhī ʾūtumina after the connecting hamza drops, since there is then no reason to change it into a long vowel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r1.anchor: فقرأه الجمهور بكسر ذال الذي وبهمزة ساكنة بعد كسرة الذال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r2.speaker: ورش
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r2.claim: Warsh from Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Abū Jaʿfar read al-ladhītumina, changing the hamza to wāw under the passive-form vowel and then wāw to yāʾ after the connecting hamza drops.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r2.anchor: وقرأه ورش عن نافع ، وأبو عمرو ، وأبو جعفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r3.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r3.claim: Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim reads alladhī awtumin, using wāw to represent the hamza following a ḍamma.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r4.claim: These recitational differences concern oral delivery and do not conflict with the written consonantal text.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125/r4.anchor: وهذا الاختلاف راجع إلى وجه الأداء فلا مخالفة فيه لرسم المصحف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r1.claim: The general ban on concealing testimony is a second charge to witnesses, summarizing the commands to write justly and not refuse testimony.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r1.anchor: وصاية ثانية للشهداء تجمع الشهادات في جميع الأحوال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r2.claim: A prohibition repeats whenever the occasion to commit the act arises; witnesses should disclose what they know whenever needed and may act earlier if absence, forgetfulness, or death could erase the evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r2.anchor: فلذلك كان حقا على من تحمل شهادة بحق ألا يكتمه عند عروض إعلانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r3.claim: The earlier commands to make testimony clear and to accept an invitation show the law’s concern to reveal rights, not suppress them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r3.anchor: وأنه حرض الشاهد على الحضور للإشهاد إذا طلب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r4.claim: The Prophet calls the best witnesses those who bring their testimony before being asked; Mālik records it, and Muslim and the four Sunan collections transmit it from him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r4.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ألا أخبركم بخير الشهداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r5.claim: The author says this interpretation is supported by both transmitted evidence and reasoning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r5.anchor: فهذا وجه تفسير الآية تظاهر فيه الأثر والنظر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r6.claim: In a sound report from Abū Hurayra, the Prophet praises the earliest generations and then warns of later people who testify before being asked.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p125#2/r6.anchor: ثم يخلف قوم يشهدون قبل أن يستشهدوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p128/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p128/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p128/r1.claim: Calling the concealer’s heart sinful attributes the act to the mental faculty that intends it; the heart signifies perception, emotion, and intention, which causes the committed sin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p128/r1.anchor: والقلب اسم للإدراك والانفعالات النفسية والنوايا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p128/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p128/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p128/r2.claim: The verse about concealing testimony threatens punishment: because only ignorance could prevent a capable God from requiting action, divine knowledge implies judgment.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r1.claim: After recommending documentation and witnessing, the verse addresses circumstances preventing writing and substitutes a pledged security; travel is the common case, but other impediments, including a debtor's unreliable standing, also justify a pledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r1.anchor: وجعل لها الرهن ونص من أحوال العذر على السفر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r2.claim: The Prophet pledged his armor to a Jewish seller who lent him barley; when the seller alleged he meant to take his money, the Prophet swore he was trustworthy in heaven and earth and said he would repay if entrusted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r2.anchor: وقد رهن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم درعه عند يهودي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r3.speaker: جمهور من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r3.claim: Most scholars say the Qurʾān establishes pledges in travel, while the Prophetic report establishes them at home; Ibn ʿAṭiyya agrees but says the verse's travel scenario is only an example, so its general meaning includes home circumstances.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r3.anchor: فالرهن في الحضر موجود في الآية بالمعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r4.speaker: الضحاك ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Mujāhid confine both pledges and trust to travel; al-Ṭabarī weakens their restriction on pledges because of the sound hadith but supports their restriction on trust. Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects both limits, saying trust is common and sound at home too.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r4.anchor: والصحيح ضعف القول في الفصلين بل يقع الائتمان في الحضر كثيرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r5.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r5.claim: Most readers have kātiban, “a writer”; Ubayy b. Kaʿb and Ibn ʿAbbās read kitāban, a verbal noun or a plural of writer, and Mujāhid and Abū al-ʿĀliya explain it as absence of writing tools or supplies. Ibn ʿAbbās also has a plural reading for writers, and Abū al-ʿĀliya reads kutuban, books; Ibn ʿAṭiyya accepts the readings except insofar as the consonantal text favors one.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب وابن عباس «كتابا» بكسر الكاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r1.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r1.claim: They and most scholars read rihān; Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read ruhun, sometimes with a lightened hāʾ, and groups read both forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r1.anchor: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وجمهور من العلماء «فرهان»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r2.claim: Rahn in Arabic can mean to remain or continue; a poem's “meat and bread are lasting” illustrates the sense. Jurists consequently void a pledge when it leaves the creditor's possession, since it departs from its defining state.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r2.anchor: رهن الشيء في كلام العرب معناه: دام واستمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r3.claim: Arhana can mean to bid heavily for an item until obtaining it at a high price, illustrated by a poem about a noble she-camel for which dinars were paid.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r3.anchor: ويقال أرهن في السلعة إذا غالى فيها حتى أخذها بكثير الثمن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r4.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r4.claim: Some attest arhantu irhānan for collateral, while Abū ʿAlī distinguishes arhantu for outbidding from rahantu for loan or sale; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says rahantu rahnan is standard without disagreement, with the verbal noun transferred to the pledged object and treated as a noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r4.anchor: بلا خلاف في البيع والقرض: رهنت رهنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r5.claim: The pledge noun's plural takes kasra like nouns and lexicalized verbal nouns; in “I pledged a garment,” the verb takes an object rather than an internal verbal noun. Abū ʿAlī nevertheless allows arhantu, though rahantu is more frequent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r5.anchor: صار فعله ينصبه نصب المفعول به لا نصب المصدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r6.claim: Poetic examples from al-Aʿshā and Hammām b. Murra attest forms from both rahana and arhāna in the pledge sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p386/r6.anchor: فهذه رويت من رهن وأما أرهن فمنه قول همام بن مرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r1.speaker: الزجاج وابن الأعرابي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r1.claim: Both rahantu and arhantu are said for pledging a security; rahantu is used for pledging one’s tongue, not arhantu.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج يقال في الرهن رهنت وأرهنت، وقاله ابن الأعرابي، ويقال رهنت لساني بكذا ولا يقال فيه أرهنت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r2.claim: The readings farhān, farhun with both vowels, and farhun with a silent hāʾ are respectively a plural, another plural pattern, and a lightened form of rahn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ «فرهن» بضم الراء والهاء فهو جمع رهن،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r3.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r3.claim: He knows no broken plural of rahn for a small number; if one existed, its expected pattern would be afʿul, but usage relies on other plural patterns.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r3.anchor: وتكسير رهن على أقل العدد لم أعلمه جاء، ولو جاء لكان قياسه أفعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r4.speaker: الطبري والفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r4.claim: They report an interpretation of rahnun with damma as plural of rihān, itself a plural of rahn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r4.anchor: قال الطبري: تأول قوم أن «رهنا» بضم الراء والهاء جمع رهان، فهو جمع جمع، وحكاه الزجاج عن الفراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r5.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r5.claim: He offers an analogy for a plural-of-plural reading, then rejects relying on it because Sibawayh did not regard such formations as productive without attested usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r5.anchor: ثم ضعف أبو علي هذا القياس وقال إن سيبويه لا يرى جمع الجمع مطردا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r6.claim: The word maqbuḍa implies the pledge passes into the mortgagee’s possession; possession by the mortgagee or the mortgagee’s agent is unanimously valid.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r6.anchor: مقبوضة يقتضي بينونة المرتهن بالرهن، وأجمع الناس على صحة قبض المرتهن، وكذلك على قبض وكيله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r7.speaker: مالك وجميع أصحابه وجمهور العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r7.claim: They count delivery of the pledge to a neutral custodian as valid possession; al-Ḥakam, Qatada, and others disagree, and the author prefers the majority’s reasoning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r7.anchor: واختلفوا في قبض عدل يوضع الرهن على يديه، فقال مالك وجميع أصحابه وجمهور العلماء قبض العدل قبض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r8.speaker: الحكم بن عتيبة وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r8.claim: They hold that placement of the pledge with a neutral custodian does not count as possession; the author says the majority view is stronger in meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p387/r8.anchor: وقال الحكم بن عتيبة وأبو الخطاب قتادة بن دعامة وغيرهما: ليس قبض العدل بقبض، وقول الجمهور أصح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r1.claim: The trust clause conditionally binds the debtor to repay; the imperative is obligatory, supported by consensus, judicial enforcement, and sound reports forbidding appropriation of another’s property.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r1.anchor: شرط ربط به وصية الذي عليه الحق بالأداء، وقوله فليؤد أمر بمعنى الوجوب بقرينة الإجماع على وجوب أداء الديون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r2.claim: Amānatihi can name the debt owed, called a trust because it is related to the debtor, or mean the trust itself, so the wording means to preserve one’s honor by repaying it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r2.anchor: وأضافها إلى الذي عليه الدين من حيث لها إليه نسبة، ويحتمل أن يريد بالأمانة نفس المصدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r3.speaker: أحمد بن موسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r3.claim: He labels the raised-alif reading attributed to Abu Bakr from ʿĀṣim as the reading alladhī utumina.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r3.anchor: وقرأ عاصم فيما روى عنه أبو بكر الذي اؤتمن برفع الألف ويشير بالضم إلى الهمزة، قال أحمد بن موسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r4.speaker: أحمد بن موسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r4.claim: He calls that reading label erroneous; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the standard form read by the other reciters is correct and alone permissible, while Abu ʿAlī defends Ahmad’s position.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r4.anchor: وهذه الترجمة غلط، وقرأ الباقون بالذال مكسورة وبعدها همزة ساكنة بغير إشمام، وهذا هو الصواب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r5.speaker: سليم عن حمزة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r5.claim: Sulaym transmits an imāla-like rounding of the hamza to ḍamma in this word, which the author also calls impermissible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r5.anchor: وروى سليم عن حمزة إشمام الهمزة الضم، وهذا خطأ أيضا لا يجوز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r6.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r6.claim: Abu ʿAlī approves Ahmad ibn Musa’s entire reading position and argues in its favor, contrary to the author’s judgment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r6.anchor: وصوب أبو علي هذا القول كله الذي لأحمد بن موسى واحتج له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r7.claim: Suppressing testimony is forbidden, as indicated by the threat; the duty applies when a witness fears a right will be lost.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r7.anchor: ولا تكتموا الشهادة نهي على الوجوب بعدة قرائن، منها الوعيد وموضع النهي هو حيث يخاف الشاهد ضياع حق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r8.claim: A witness should testify whenever summoned and inform the parties when asked, rather than reserving the information for a governor, so the wrongdoer may turn back.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس على الشاهد أن يشهد حيثما استشهد ويخبر حيثما استخبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya limits that advice by circumstances: under corrupt conditions, giving testimony in an ineffective venue may aid falsehood and conceal the truth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r9.anchor: وهذا عندي بحسب قرينة حال الشاهد والمشهود فيه والنازلة، لا سيما مع فساد الزمن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r10.claim: Athim qalbuhu describes the sin attaching to concealment; qalbuhu may be the subject of athim, the subject whose clause completes the predicate, or a partitive apposition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388/r10.anchor: وآثم معناه قد تعلق به الحكم اللاحق عن المعصية في كتمان الشهادة، وإعرابه أنه خبر «إن» ، وقلبه فاعل ب آثم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r1.claim: The heart is singled out because concealment is its act and because the heart is the bodily morsel whose soundness makes the body sound, as the Prophet said.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r1.anchor: وإذ هو المضغة التي بصلاحها يصلح الجسد كما قال عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r2.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads qalbahu in the accusative; Makki calls this an explanatory accusative but weakens it because the noun is definite.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة «فإنه آثم قلبه» بنصب الباء، قال مكي هو على التفسير ثم ضعفه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r3.claim: The closing statement that God knows all deeds is a threat, although its wording can encompass promise as well as threat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p388#2/r3.anchor: والله بما تعملون عليم توعد وإن كان لفظها يعم الوعيد والوعد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r1.claim: Travel is singled out because writers and witnesses are less commonly available there; when written documentation is unavailable, take a pledge in hand.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r1.anchor: إنما خص السفر لأن الأغلب عدم الكاتب والشاهد فيه ومقصود الكلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and ʿAbd al-Warith read ruhun without alif; ʿAbd al-Warith also has a sukun for ease of pronunciation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعبد الوارث فرهن بضم الراء والهاء من غير ألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r3.speaker: نافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r3.claim: Nafiʿ, ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read rihān with alif; Ibn Qutayba says this is a plural of rahn, whereas ruhun is a plural of rihān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341#2/r3.anchor: قرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزه والكسائي ﴿ فرهان ﴾ بكسر الراء وفتح الهاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r1.claim: If travelers cannot find a scribe, or even paper, ink, or pen, they should take a pledge in the creditor's possession in place of writing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r1.anchor: أو وجدوه ولم يجد قرطاسا أو دواة أو قلما فرهن مقبوضة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي والجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r2.claim: They infer from 'pledges taken' that a pledge is not binding until it is taken into possession.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r2.anchor: على أن الرهن لا يلزم إلا بالقبض، كما هو مذهب الشافعي والجمهور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r3.speaker: رواية عن أحمد وطائفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r3.claim: They infer that the pledge must be held by the creditor, the pledgee.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r3.anchor: على أنه لا بد أن يكون الرهن مقبوضا في يد المرتهن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد وغيرهم من السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r4.claim: Some early authorities infer from the verse that pledges are lawful only while traveling.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r4.anchor: على أنه لا يكون الرهن مشروعا إلا في السفر، قاله مجاهد وغيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r5.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r5.claim: A report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections says the Prophet died with his armor pledged to a Jew for thirty wasqs of barley as food for his family; variants identify the Jew as from Medina or Abu al-Shahm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727#2/r5.anchor: توفي ودرعه مرهونة عند يهودي على ثلاثين وسقا من شعير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r1.claim: He says the permission to trust one another superseded the preceding direction; Ibn Abi Hatim gives the report with a good chain.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r2.speaker: الشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r2.claim: When parties trust one another, they may omit writing or witnesses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r2.anchor: وقال الشعبي: إذا ائتمن بعضكم (1) بعضا فلا بأس ألا تكتبوا أو لا تشهدوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r3.claim: The person trusted to repay or return property is the one commanded to fulfill the trust; a report from Samura says the hand is responsible for what it takes until it returns it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r3.anchor: يعنى: المؤتمن، كما جاء في الحديث الذي رواه الإمام أحمد وأهل السنن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r4.claim: Concealing testimony means hiding, suppressing, or withholding it; Ibn Abbas and others treat false testimony and withholding testimony as major sins.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p728/r5.claim: He explains that the heart of someone who conceals testimony is wicked; Ibn Kathir links this to 5:106 and the command in 4:135 to uphold justice.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r1.claim: They read the word as رهن.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير , وأبو عمرو : فرهن

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r2.speaker: الباقون
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r2.claim: The other readers read the word as رهان.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r3.claim: One view reserves rahn for pledges of property and rihān for horses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r3.anchor: أن الرهن في الأموال , والرهان في الخيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r4.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r4.claim: Rihān is a plural and rahn a plural of the plural, like thimār from thamar.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r4.anchor: أن الرهان جمع , والرهن جمع الجمع مثل ثمار وثمر , قاله الكسائي , والفراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r5.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r5.claim: Taking possession completes a pledge; before possession the pledge is incomplete.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r5.anchor: أن القبض من تمام الرهن , وهو قبل القبض غير تام , قاله الشافعي , وأبو حنيفة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r6.speaker: مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r6.claim: Possession is a requisite of a pledge, which is complete before possession.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r6.anchor: لأنه من لوازم الرهن , وهو قبل القبض التام , قاله مالك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r7.claim: Travel is not a condition for a valid pledge: the Prophet pledged his armor to the Jewish Abu al-Shahm while resident in Medina.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r7.anchor: لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رهن درعه عند أبي الشحم اليهودي بالمدينة وهي حضر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r8.claim: Absence of a scribe or witness is also not a condition for pledging, since a pledge is an added security.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r8.anchor: ولا عدم الكاتب والشاهد شرطا فيه لأنه زيادة وثيقة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r9.claim: Mutual trust means dispensing with a scribe, witnesses, and a pledge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r9.anchor: يعني بغير كاتب ولا شاهد ولا رهن

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r10.claim: The person entrusted must pay what is owed and not delay it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r10.anchor: يعني في أداء الحق وترك المطل به

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r11.claim: The debtor must fear God by concealing none of the creditor's right.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r11.anchor: في ألا يكتم من الحق شيئا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r12.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r12.claim: The phrase “his heart is sinful” means his heart is depraved.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p358/r13.claim: Alternatively, the heart has incurred the sin of concealing testimony.

MUQATIL:2:283/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:283/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:283/r1.claim: When traveling without a scribe or writing materials, the debtor should provide the creditor with a held pledge; if trusted without collateral, he must repay the debt entrusted to him and fear God.
MUQATIL:2:283/r1.anchor: فليرتهن الذى عليه الحق من المطلوب،

MUQATIL:2:283/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:283/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:283/r2.claim: Witnesses must testify accurately before the judge and not conceal testimony; whoever hides it sins in his heart, and God knows whether testimony is given or suppressed.
MUQATIL:2:283/r2.anchor: فلا تكتموا الشهادة، قال: { ومن يكتمها } ولا يشهد بها عند الحاكم،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r1.speaker: مكي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r1.claim: Makki reads رهٰن as رهان; both readings are plurals of رهن, first a verbal noun later declined as a noun.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r1.anchor: فرهان مكى و أبو عمرو أى فالذى يستوثق به رهن وكلاهما جمع رهن

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr shares the reading رهان, with رهٰن as another plural of رهن.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r2.anchor: فرهان مكى و أبو عمرو أى فالذى يستوثق به رهن وكلاهما جمع رهن

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r3.claim: Travel creates the likelihood that writing and witnesses are unavailable, so collateral is guidance for preserving property in their place.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r3.anchor: ولما كان السفر مظنة لا عواز الكتب والاشهاد أمر على سبيل الإرشاد إلى حفظ المال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r4.claim: The word مقبوضة makes possession a condition for a valid pledge; this rejects Mālik's view that offer and acceptance alone suffice.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r4.anchor: اشتراط القبض لا كما زعم مالك أن الرهن يصح بالإيجاب والقبول بدون القبض

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r5.claim: If the creditor trusts the debtor, no writing, witnesses, or pledge is needed; the debtor must repay the entrusted debt and not deny it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r5.anchor: فإن أمن بعض الدائنين بعض المديونين بحسن ظنه به فلم يتوثق بالكتابة والشهود والرهن

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r6.claim: Calling the debt an amanah reflects the lender's trust in leaving it unpledged even though the debt remains guaranteed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r6.anchor: وسمى الدين أمانة وهو مضمون لإئتمانه عليه بترك الارتهان منه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r7.claim: The command not to conceal testimony addresses witnesses.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r7.anchor: ﴿ ولا تكتموا الشهادة ﴾ هذا خطاب للشهود

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r8.claim: The phrase إثم قلبه may make the heart the agent of sin or make it the subject of a fronted predicate; attribution to the heart emphasizes that concealment is inwardly hidden.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r8.anchor: ارتفع قلبه بآثم على الفاعلية كأنه قيل فإنه يأثم قلبه أو بالابتداء وآثم خبر مقدم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r9.claim: The heart is named because concealment begins inside it; deeds attributed to their organ are more emphatic, and the heart leads the body, so the sin occupies the self's noblest place.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r9.anchor: لأن كتمان الشهادة أن يضمرها فى القلب ولا يتكلم بها فلما كان إثما مقترفا مكتسبا بالقلب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r10.claim: Making this a sin of the heart marks it among the gravest sins, since faith and disbelief, the basis of good and evil, are also acts of the heart.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r10.anchor: ألا ترى أن أصل الحسنات والسيآت الإيمان والكفر وهما من أفعال القلوب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās names associating partners with God, false testimony, and concealing testimony among the greatest major sins.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r11.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما أكبر الكبائر الإشراك بالله وشهادة الزور وكتمان الشهادة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r12.claim: God knows whether testimony is concealed or disclosed, and nothing is hidden from Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138#2/r12.anchor: ﴿ والله بما تعملون ﴾ من كتمان الشهادة وإظهارها ﴿ عليم ﴾ لا يخفى عليه شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r1.claim: When writing is prevented by an excuse, a pledge protects property; travel is common, but any impediment qualifies, including a busy time or nighttime, and concern about the debtor may justify security.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r1.anchor: وجعل لها الرهن، ونص من أحوال العذر على السفر الذي هو غالب الأعذار

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r2.claim: The Prophet pledged his armor with a Jewish seller for barley; he insisted that he was trustworthy and would repay, yet died while the armor remained pledged.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r2.anchor: فمات ودرعه مرهونة صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r3.speaker: جمهور من العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r3.claim: The majority permit pledges during travel by Qurʾānic text and in settled places by the Prophet's practice; al-Qurṭubī also reads the verse by analogy to any excuse.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r3.anchor: قال جمهور من العلماء: الرهن في السفر بنص التنزيل، وفي الحضر ثابت بسنة الرسول

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r4.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وداود
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r4.claim: Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Dāwūd restrict pledges to travel, but al-Qurṭubī rejects their inference because the verse describes the usual case rather than prohibiting pledges elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r4.anchor: سوى مجاهد والضحاك وداود، متمسكين بالآية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r5.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r5.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet bought food on credit from a Jew and pledged his iron armor; Ibn ʿAbbās reports it remained pledged at his death for thirty measures of barley.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r5.anchor: عن عائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اشترى من يهودي طعاما إلى أجل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r6.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r6.claim: Most readers have the singular 'writer'; Ibn ʿAbbās and others read a plural understood as writing materials, scribes, or lack of tools, with grammarians offering different analyses.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r7.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r7.claim: Al-Naḥḥās calls the alternative reading rare; Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds it apt for varied cases, and al-Qurṭubī says both readings work apart from the codex spelling.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283/r7.anchor: قال النحاس: هذه القراءة شاذة والعامة على خلافها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read rahun; other readings include ruhun and ruhan, with grammarians disputing whether these are plural forms or collective nouns.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير «فرهن» بضم الراء والهاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r2.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r2.claim: Al-Mahdawī parses 'pledges' as a subject with an omitted predicate: possessed pledges suffice for security.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r3.claim: A pledge is property retained as security so a creditor can recover from its price or proceeds if collection from the debtor fails; the Arabic root also means permanence and continuity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r3.anchor: معنى الرهن: احتباس العين وثيقة بالحق ليستوفى الحق من ثمنها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī says the small plural of rahn is unattested; if it existed, its pattern would be afʿāl, as in kalb and aklab.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: وتكسير «رهن» على أقل العدد لم أعلمه جاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r1.speaker: أبو علي وأبو زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī and Abū Zayd distinguish forms of the pledge verb: arhantu is used for bidding high, while raḥantu is used for loans and sales.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r1.anchor: وقال أبو علي: أرهنت في المغالاة، وأما في القرض والبيع فرهنت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r2.speaker: الزجاج وابن الأعرابي والأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj, Ibn al-Aʿrābī, and al-Akhfash also allow both raḥantu and arhantu for pledging.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يقال في الرهن: رهنت وأرهنت وقاله ابن الأعرابي والأخفش

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن همام السلولي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r3.claim: A verse by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hammām al-Salūlī uses arhantu; most transmitters retain that form, while al-Aṣmaʿī reads a present-tense verb after the past and explains the wāw as circumstantial.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r3.anchor: قال عبد الله بن همام السلولي: فلما خشيت أظافيرهم نجوت وأرهنتهم مالكا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r4.claim: The pledged person is the one receiving the pledge; an object may be called marhūn or rahīn, a woman rahīna, and rahantu is standard for pledging in a sale or loan.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r4.anchor: ويقال بلا خلاف في البيع والقرض: رهنت رهنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī adopts the view that a pledge ends if it voluntarily returns to the pledgor, following the requirement that it be possessed; Abū Ḥanīfa exempts return as a loan or deposit, while al-Shāfiʿī preserves the earlier possession.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r5.anchor: قلت هذا هو المعتمد عندنا في أن الرهن متى رجع إلى الراهن باختيار المرتهن بطل الرهن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r6.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says a pledge made verbally but never physically possessed creates no legal effect, because the verse predicates the ruling on possession.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r6.anchor: قال الشافعي: لم يجعل الله الحكم إلا برهن موصوف بالقبض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r7.speaker: المالكية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r7.claim: The Mālikīs say the contract binds the pledgor and require delivery; possession completes the pledge's benefit, while two other schools make it a condition of bindingness and validity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#3/r7.anchor: وقالت المالكية: يلزم الرهن بالعقد ويجبر الراهن على دفع الرهن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r1.speaker: المالكية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r1.claim: The Mālikīs support the pledge's binding contract by commands to fulfill contracts and promises, and the Prophetic rule that believers fulfill their conditions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r1.anchor: وهذا شرط، فالقبض عندنا شرط في كمال فائدته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r2.speaker: جمهور العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r2.claim: Possession by a neutral custodian counts as receipt because the custodian represents the creditor; Ibn Abī Laylā, Qatāda, al-Ḥakam, and ʿAṭāʾ require the creditor to hold it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r2.anchor: وقول الجمهور أصح من جهة المعنى لأنه إذا صار عند العدل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r3.claim: If collateral with a neutral custodian is lost, neither creditor nor custodian is liable: the creditor never possessed it and the custodian is a trustee.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r3.anchor: والأمين غير ضامن. العاشرة لما قال تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r4.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r4.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir argues that a Ḥanafī exception allowing two creditors jointly to take a plot as collateral concedes that a share in common property may be pledged.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r4.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وهذا إجازة رهن المشاع لأن كل واحد منهما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r5.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r5.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir considers pledging jointly owned property valid just as selling it is valid; al-Qurṭubī's school permits it against Abū Ḥanīfa's school.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r5.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: رهن المشاع جائز كما يجوز بيعه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r6.claim: The Mālikīs permit pledging a debt owed by another: anything saleable may be collateral, and a debt has value, though opponents say it cannot be physically possessed or directly realized.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r6.anchor: الحادية عشرة ورهن ما في الذمة جائز عند علمائنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r7.claim: Al-Bukhārī transmits from Abū Hurayra the Prophet's rule that an animal pledged as collateral may be ridden and its milk drunk in return for the expense borne by the user.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#4/r7.anchor: روى البخاري عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r1.speaker: الخطابي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r1.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī says the first wording does not identify whether the pledgor, creditor, or custodian may ride and milk the pledged animal.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r1.anchor: قال الخطابي: هذا كلام مبهم ليس في نفس اللفظ بيان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r2.speaker: أحمد وإسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r2.claim: A more explicit Abū Hurayra report says the creditor who feeds a pledged animal may ride or drink its milk in proportion to the expense; Aḥmad and Isḥāq adopt that rule.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r2.anchor: وهو قول أحمد وإسحاق: أن المرتهن ينتفع من الرهن بالحلب والركوب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r3.speaker: أبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r3.claim: Abū Thawr permits a creditor who maintained neglected collateral to ride it or use an enslaved servant; al-Awzāʿī and al-Layth share this view.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r3.anchor: وقال أبو ثور: إذا كان الراهن ينفق عليه لم ينتفع به المرتهن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r4.claim: A report says a pledge cannot be foreclosed and its owner receives its yield and bears its loss; Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, al-Shaʿbī, and Ibn Sīrīn hold that benefits belong to its owner, who pays upkeep.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r5.speaker: الخطابي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r5.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī considers the view that collateral's benefits belong to its owner strongest, supported by the explicit wording about its yield and loss.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r5.anchor: قال الخطابي: وهو أولى الأقوال وأصحها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r6.speaker: الطحاوي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r6.claim: Al-Ṭaḥāwī argues the permissive benefit report came before the prohibition of usury; al-Shaʿbī argues it was abrogated, since even a pledged enslaved woman may not be used.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r6.anchor: وقال الطحاوي: كان ذلك وقت كون الربا مباحا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r7.speaker: ابن عبد البر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr says scholars agree the pledged animal's milk and use belong to its owner; use without permission is barred, while permission raises issues of unknown benefit and usury.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#5/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عبد البر وقد أجمعوا أن لبن الرهن وظهره للراهن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r1.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r1.claim: Ibn Khuwayzimandād says a creditor may stipulate use of collateral in a sale or lease, but not a loan, where it would be a loan yielding benefit and thus usury.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r1.anchor: وقال ابن خويز منداد: ولو شرط المرتهن الانتفاع بالرهن فلذلك حالتان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r2.claim: A pledge may not be stipulated to become the creditor's property if the debtor misses the due date; this pre-Islamic foreclosure practice was abolished by the Prophetic report.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r2.anchor: لا يجوز غلق الرهن، وهو أن يشترط المرتهن أنه له بحقه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r3.claim: The report is read with an indicative nominative ending: the pledge does not become foreclosed; the Arabic expression also describes a closed door or unredeemed collateral.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#6/r3.anchor: هكذا قيدناه برفع القاف على الخبر، أي ليس يغلق الرهن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r1.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r1.claim: Abū ʿUmar says a connected chain for the report may be mistaken: Ismāʿīl did not hear from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb directly, but via weak ʿAbbād; the report's basis is mursal.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r1.anchor: قال أبو عمر: لم يسمعه إسماعيل من ابن أبي ذئب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r2.claim: The report's basis among hadith critics is mursal, although it has many connected routes they criticize; the wording about yield and loss is also disputed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r2.anchor: وأصل هذا الحديث عند أهل العلم بالنقل مرسل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r3.claim: Collateral growth inseparable from the property, such as fattening or offspring, follows the pledge; crops, milk, wool, and fruit do not unless stipulated because they are independently treated for alms.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r3.anchor: وما عدا ذلك من غلة وثمرة ولبن وصوف فلا يدخل فيه إلا أن يشترطه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r4.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r4.claim: Mālik and many jurists give a secured creditor priority over other creditors when a debtor not declared insolvent pledges an asset; al-Qurṭubī rejects another report giving all creditors a share.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#7/r4.anchor: ويكون المرتهن أحق بالرهن من الغرماء قاله مالك وجماعة من الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r1.claim: If the debtor is trusted, the creditor must allow payment without delay; the imperative is obligatory by consensus, enforceable judgments, and sound reports.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r1.anchor: وهو أمر معناه الوجوب، بقرينة الإجماع على وجوب أداء الديون

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r2.claim: 'His trust' refers to the debt owed by the debtor, named as a verbal noun and attributed to him, as in the verse about not giving property to the foolish.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r2.anchor: الأمانة مصدر سمى به الشيء الذي في الذمة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a witness must testify wherever summoned and disclose testimony wherever questioned, rather than reserve it only for a ruler.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: على الشاهد أن يشهد حيثما استشهد، ويخبر حيثما استخبر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r4.claim: The ban on concealing testimony is obligatory when a right may be lost; testimony is a collective duty, and a claimant's request makes it incumbent on needed witnesses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r4.anchor: نهى الشاهد عن أن يضر بكتمان الشهادة، وهو نهي على الوجوب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r5.claim: The heart is singled out because concealment begins there; naming the part for the whole intensifies the warning, and the clause admits several grammatical parses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r5.anchor: خص القلب بالذكر إذ الكتم من أفعاله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r6.speaker: الكيا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r6.claim: Al-Kiyā says intending to withhold testimony and then not speaking makes sin apply to resolve and speech; calling the heart sinful is forceful rhetoric.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#8/r6.anchor: وقال الكيا: لما عزم على ألا يؤديها وترك أداءها باللسان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r1.claim: Writing and testimony protect social relations from disputes, denial, and demanding more than is owed; uncertain sales, gambling, and wine are barred because they breed hostility.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r1.anchor: لمراعاة صلاح ذات البين ونفى التنازع المؤدي إلى فساد ذات البين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r2.claim: Following God's commands and prohibitions brings well-being in this world and religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r2.anchor: فمن تأدب بأدب الله في أوامره وزواجره حاز صلاح الدنيا والدين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r3.claim: The Prophet says God repays for one who takes people's money intending repayment and destroys the one who takes it intending to squander it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r3.anchor: روى البخاري عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r4.speaker: ميمونة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r4.claim: Maymūna reports that God helps a person who borrows intending repayment; another report warns debt can frighten people after they felt secure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r4.anchor: وروى النسائي: عن ميمونة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنها استدانت، فقيل: يا أم المؤمنين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r5.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r5.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's prayer seeking refuge from anxiety, incapacity, miserliness, the burden of debt, and domination by others; scholars explain the burden as inability to repay.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#9/r5.anchor: وروى البخاري عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعاء ذكره

SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r1.claim: The common reading kātiban is an active participle, ‘a scribe.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ولم تجدوا كاتبا }: العامة على " كاتبا " اسم فاعل.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r2.speaker: أبي ومجاهد وأبو العالية
