SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r2.claim: Ubayy, Mujahid, and Abu al-Aliyya read kitāban, which can mean writing as a verbal noun or be a plural of kātib.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبي ومجاهد وأبو العالية: " كتابا " ، وفيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنه مصدر أي ذا كتابة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attributes kitāban only to Ubayy and Ibn Abbas; Ibn Abbas asks what if a scribe exists but no paper or ink, favoring ‘writing’ over ‘scribe.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r3.anchor: ونقل الزمخشري هذه القراءة عن أبي وابن عباس فقط، وقال: " وقال ابن عباس: أرأيت إن وجدت الكاتب ولم تجد الصحيفة والدواة ".

SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak read kitāban as a plural, reasoning that each case has its own scribe.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والضحاك: " كتابا " على الجمع، اعتبارا بأن كل نازلة لها كاتب.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliyya reads kutuban, plural of kitāb, in view of the many separate cases.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو العالية: " كتبا " جمع كتاب، اعتبارا بالنوازل،

SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari’s quotation from Ibn Abbas supports that reading and shows the verse means the written record rather than a scribe.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r6.anchor: قلت: قول ابن عباس: " أرأيت إن وجدت الكاتب الخ " ترجيح للقراءة المروية عنه واستبعاد لقراءة غيره/ " كاتبا " ، يعني أن المراد الكتاب لا الكاتب.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r7.claim: Rihān may be a result clause with an omitted verb, a subject with an omitted predicate, or a predicate with an omitted subject such as ‘the document.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r7.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أنه مرفوع بفعل محذوف، أي: فيكفي [عن] ذلك رهن مقبوضة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read ruhan with ḍamma; the others read rihānan with kasra and a long alif, with a reported hāʾ-sukūn variant.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: " فرهن " بضم الراء والهاء، والباقون " فرهان " بكسر الراء وألف بعد الهاء،

SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir’s form is a plural of rahn on the pattern fuʿul, like saqf/suqūf; al-Akhfash supplies other examples though the pattern is rare.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r9.anchor: فأما قراءة ابن كثير فجمع رهن، وفعل يجمع على فعل نحو: سقف وسقف.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r10.claim: Abu Amr cites Qanab’s poem as evidence for ruhan and says he chose it to distinguish ordinary pledges from horse-racing wagers, following transmitted reading.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283/r10.anchor: وأنشد أبو عمرو حجة لقراءته قول قعنب

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers ruhan because it matches the consonantal outline of the codex, has a sound meaning, and is a transmitted recitation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r1.anchor: قال: " وهذه القراءة وافقت المصحف، وما وافق المصحف وصح معناه، وقرأت به القراء فهو المختار ".

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r2.claim: The written form has no alif after hāʾ although fuʿul plurals are rare; Abu Amr says rihān is otherwise known only for horses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r2.anchor: قلت: إن الرسم الكريم " فرهن " دون ألف بعد الهاء، مع أن الزجاج يقول: " إن فعلا جمع فعل قليل "

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r3.speaker: يونس
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r3.claim: Yunus says both rahn and rihān are Arabic, with rahn more usual for a pledge and rihān more usual for horses; poetry also supports rahn.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r3.anchor: وقال يونس: " الرهن والرهان عربيان، والرهن في الرهن أكثر، والرهان في الخيل أكثر "

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ and his teacher analyze rahn as plural of rihān and rihān as plural of rahn, a double plural; Sibawayh’s school considers plural-of-plural formation irregular.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: إن رهنا جمع رهان، ورهان جمع رهن، فهو جمع الجمع، كما قالوا في ثمار جمع ثمر، وثمر جمع ثمار، وإليه ذهب الفراء وشيخه

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r5.claim: The majority’s rihān is a regular, common plural of rahn on the faʿāl pattern; hāʾ may be made quiescent for ease.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r5.anchor: وأما قراءة الباقين " رهان فرهان جمع " رهن " وفعل وفعال مطرد كثير

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r6.claim: Rahn originally is the verbal noun of rahana, giving an item as collateral to someone.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r6.anchor: والرهن في الأصل مصدر رهنت، يقال: رهنت زيدا ثوبا أرهنه رهنا أي: دفعته إليه رهنا عنده،

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r7.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r7.claim: Al-Farraʾ distinguishes rahana from arhana, the latter meaning to give an item for someone else to pawn.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r7.anchor: وأرهنت زيدا ثوبا أي: دفعته إليه ليرهنه، ففرقوا بين فعل وأفعل.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r8.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ treats rahana and arhana as synonymous and adduces a Hamam al-Saluli verse; al-Asmaʿi rejects that transmission and reads the phrase as circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r8.anchor: وعند الفراء رهنته وأرهنته بمعنى، واحتج بقول همام السلولي:

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r9.speaker: الأصمعي
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r9.claim: Al-Asmaʿi rejects the transmitted wording, preferring ‘wa-arhanuhū Mālikan’ with a circumstantial wāw and an implied subject.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r9.anchor: وأنكر الأصمعي هذه الرواية وقال: " إنما الرواية: وأرهنهم مالكا " ، والواو للحال

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r10.claim: Arhana can also mean bidding heavily on an item until it is bought at a high price, as in the cited verse.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: أرهن في السلعة إذا غالى فيها حتى أخذها بكثير الثمن

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r11.claim: One says rahantu lisānī, ‘I pledged my tongue,’ but not arhantu in this usage.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#2/r11.anchor: ويقال: رهنت لساني بكذا، ولا يقال فيه " أرهنت "

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r1.claim: Rahn can denote the pledged object by transferring a verbal noun to the passive-object meaning, like ‘this is God’s creation’ or ‘a dirham minted by the ruler.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r1.anchor: هذا خلق الله [لقمان: 11]، و " درهم ضرب الأمير " ، فإذا قلت: " رهنت زيدا ثوبا رهنا " فرهنا هنا مصدر فقط،

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r2.claim: In ‘I pledged a garment as a pledge,’ rahnan is only a verbal noun; in ‘I pledged a pledge,’ it can be the object meaning the pledged item, or an emphatic verbal noun with a second object omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r2.anchor: فإذا قلت: " رهنت زيدا ثوبا رهنا " فرهنا هنا مصدر فقط، وإذا قلت " رهنت زيدا رهنا " فهو هنا مفعول به

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r3.claim: Rahn has no commonly used broken plural for paucity: its frequent plurals ruhan and rihān replace the expected arhān.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r3.anchor: و " رهن " مما استغنى فيه بجمع كثرته عن جمع قلته، وذلك أن قياسه في القلة أفعل كفلس وأفلس،

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r4.claim: The root meaning of rahn is permanence and stability; an established thing is described as rāhin.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r4.anchor: وأصل الرهن: الثبوت والاستقرار، يقال: رهن الشيء، فهو راهن إذا دام واستقر، ونعمة راهنة أي دائمة ثابتة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r5.speaker: ابن السكيت
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r5.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit’s verse uses rāhina for something lasting; food described as rāhin likewise means settled and enduring.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r5.anchor: وأنشد ابن السكيت: 1140 لا يستفيقون منها وهي راهنة إلا بهات

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r6.claim: A pledged object is called rahn because it remains and stays with the pledgee.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#3/r6.anchor: ومنه سمي المرهون " رهنا " لدوامه واستقراره عند المرتهن.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r1.claim: ‘You did not find a scribe’ may coordinate with the conditional verb, with kāna’s predicate, or be a circumstantial clause; the last two are nominative-context constructions.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r1.anchor: في هذه الجملة ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أنها عطف على فعل الشرط أي: " وإن كنتم ولم تجدوا " فتكون في محل جزم

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r2.speaker: أبي
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r2.claim: Ubayy’s transmitted reading ‘if some of you are trusted’ is passive; al-Zamakhshari explains that people vouch for the debtor’s reliability and fulfillment.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r2.anchor: قرأ أبي فيما نقله عنه الزمخشري " أومن " مبنيا للمفعول. قال الزمخشري: " أي أمنه الناس ووصفوا المديون بالأمانة والوفاء "

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari interprets the passive as the people trusting the debtor and describing him as reliable and faithful.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r3.anchor: أي أمنه الناس ووصفوا المديون بالأمانة والوفاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r4.claim: On this passive reading, baʿḍan is best treated as having a deleted preposition and an omitted complement: trusted with another’s property or debt.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r4.anchor: والظاهر نصبه/ بإسقاط الخافض على حذف مضاف أي: فإن أومن بعضكم على متاع بعض

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r5.claim: At a pause after alladhī, the hamza of uʾtumin is pronounced wāw-like because the second hamza becomes quiescent after a matching ḍamma.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r5.anchor: وذلك لأن أصله أأتمن، مثل اقتدر بهمزتين: الأولى للوصل والثانية فاء الكلمة

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r6.claim: In connected recitation, the connecting hamza drops, restoring the hamza to its original state; Warsh and al-Susi transmit a clear yāʾ instead.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r6.anchor: فأما في الدرج فتذهب همزة الوصل فتعود الهمزة إلى حالها لزوال موجب قلبها واوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r7.speaker: عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r7.claim: A reading attributed to Asim signals a ḍamma on the initial alif; Ibn Mujahid calls this transcription or labeling mistaken.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r7.anchor: وروي عن عاصم: " الذي اوتمن " برفع الألف ويشير بالضمة إلى الهمزة،

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r8.speaker: سليم عن حمزة
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r8.claim: Sulaym transmits from Hamza an ishām gesture indicating ḍamma on the hamza; the author regards these gesture-based reports as questionable.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r8.anchor: وروى سليم عن حمزة إشمام الهمزة الضم، وفي الإشارة والإشمام المذكورين نظر.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r9.speaker: عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r9.claim: Asim also has a noncanonical ‘alladh-tumin’ with the yāʾ derived from hamza assimilated into tāʾ; al-Zamakhshari rejects the analogy to اتسر because the yāʾ remains hamza-like.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r9.anchor: وقرأ عاصم أيضا في شاذة: " الذتمن " بإدغام الياء المبدلة من الهمزة في تاء الافتعال،

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r10.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r10.claim: The Shaykh notes that other authorities record اتمن and اتزر as poor dialect forms, while al-Kisaʾi reports assimilation in ريا from رؤيا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#4/r10.anchor: قد ذكره غيره أن بعضهم أبدل وأدغم: " اتمن واتزر " وأن ذلك لغة رديئة،

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r1.claim: Amānatihi may mean the entrusted property and be the direct object of ‘let him repay.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الأمانة بمعنى الشيء المؤتمن عليه فينتصب انتصاب المفعول به بقوله: " فليؤد "

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r2.claim: Alternatively it is a verbal noun with an omitted possessive construction: let him repay the debt of his trust.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون مصدرا على أصلها، وتكون على حذف مضاف، أي: فليؤد دين أمانته.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r3.claim: It cannot be an absolute object formed from the verb iʾtaman.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r3.anchor: ولا جائز أن تكون منصوبة على مصدر ائتمن

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r4.claim: The pronoun in ‘his trust’ can refer either to the creditor or to the person who was trusted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r4.anchor: والضمير في " أمانته " يحتمل أن يعود على صاحب الحق، وأن يعود على الذي ائتمن.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r5.claim: In ‘his heart is sinful,’ the pronoun may be a pronoun of the matter explained by the following clause, or may refer to ‘whoever’; the latter is apparent.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r5.anchor: في هذا الضمير وجهان، أحدهما: أنه ضمير الشأن والجملة بعده، مفسر له.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r6.claim: The clearest syntax makes ‘whoever’ the referent, ‘sinful’ the predicate, and ‘his heart’ the subject of the active participle; this is incompatible with the Basran analysis of a pronoun of the matter.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r6.anchor: أظهرها: أن الضمير في " إنه " ضمير " من " و " آثم " خبر إن، و " قلبه " فاعل بآثم

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r7.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari, Abu al-Baqa, and others make ‘sinful’ a fronted predicate and ‘his heart’ a delayed subject; the author notes a Kufi objection about a pronoun referring to a later noun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r7.anchor: أن يكون " آثم " خبرا مقدما، و " قلبه " مبتدأ مؤخرا، والجملة خبر " إن " ذكر ذلك الزمخشري وأبو البقاء وغيره

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r8.claim: Another parse makes ‘sinful’ the predicate with an implicit pronoun and ‘his heart’ a partitive apposition to that pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r8.anchor: أن يكون " آثم " خبر إن، وفيه ضمير يعود على ما تعود عليه الهاء في " إنه " ، و " قلبه " بدل من ذلك الضمير المستتر

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya makes ‘sinful’ a subject and ‘his heart’ the active participle’s subject filling the predicate position; Basrans reject such unlicensed participle government, while al-Farraʾ and al-Akhfash allow it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#5/r9.anchor: قاله ابن عطية، وهو لا يجوز عند البصريين، لأنه لا يعمل عندهم اسم الفاعل إلا إذا اعتمد على نفي أو استفهام

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r1.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r1.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads qalbahu in the accusative, as transmitted by Ibn Atiyya; one parse makes it a partitive apposition to the pronoun in inna.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: " قلبه " بالنصب، نسبها إليه ابن عطية.

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r2.claim: A second accusative analysis treats qalbahu as resembling a direct object, as in ‘a man whose face is handsome’; grammarians permit it in prose and verse, reject it entirely, or restrict it to poetry.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنه منصوب على التشبيه بالمفعول به، كقولك: " مررت برجل حسن وجهه " وفي هذا الوجه خلاف مشهور،

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r3.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r3.claim: Sibawayh permits the object-like accusative in poetry but not prose and adduces the cited poem as evidence.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r3.anchor: وهو مذهب سيبويه، وأنشد الكسائي على ذلك: 1142 أنعتها إني من نعاتها

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r4.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r4.claim: Makki and others offer a third parse, accusative of specification; Basrans object that tamyiz must be indefinite, while Kufans allow definite examples such as 2:130 and 28:85.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r4.anchor: والثالث: أنه منصوب على التمييز حكاه مكي وغيره، وضعفوه بأن التمييز لا يكون إلا نكرة،

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r5.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r5.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla also reads athima qalbuhu as a past verb with a hidden subject and ‘his heart’ as object: he made his heart sinful, using heart for the whole person.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة - فيما نقل عنه الزمخشري - " أثم قلبه " جعل " أثم " فعلا ماضيا مشدد العين،

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r6.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman reads ‘they do not conceal’ with third-person yāʾ, following the preceding mention of scribe and witness; singular wording refers to a group.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن: " ولا يكتموا " بياء الغيبة، لأن قبله غيبا وهم من ذكر في قوله: { كاتب ولا شهيد }

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r7.claim: The passage uses contrasting wordplay in ‘you transact a debt,’ matching wordplay in ‘conceal the testimony / whoever conceals it,’ and antithesis in ‘err/remember’ and ‘small/large.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r7.anchor: وقد اشتملت هذه الآيات على أنواع من البديع منها: التجنيس المغاير في " تداينتم بدين " نظائره، والمماثل في قوله: { ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها }

SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r8.speaker: السلمي
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r8.claim: Al-Sulami likewise reads ‘God knows what you do’ with third-person yāʾ, consistently with his other third-person readings.
SAMIN-DURR:2:283#6/r8.anchor: وقرأ السلمي أيضا: { والله بما تعملون } بالغيبة جريا على قراءته بالغيبة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r1.claim: Debt brings mental preoccupation, humiliation before creditors, and pressure that can lead to lying, broken promises, or broken oaths; these harms diminish its dignity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r1.anchor:
الدين شين الدين "
وروي عنه أنه قال:
" الدين هم بالليل ومذلة بالنهار "
قال علماؤنا: وإنما كان شينا ومذلة لما فيه من شغل القلب والبال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r2.claim: The Prophet sought refuge from sin and debt because indebted people may lie when speaking and break promises.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r2.anchor: إن الرجل إذا غرم حدث فكذب ووعد فأخلف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r3.claim: A believer's soul remains pledged in the grave by an unpaid debt until someone pays it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r3.anchor: نسمة المؤمن مرتهنة في قبره بدينه حتى يقضى عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r4.claim: The commands to document, witness, and take pledges decisively require safeguarding and developing wealth, against ascetics who give everything away and leave dependants to others' charity or oppression.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r4.anchor: كان ذلك نصا قاطعا على مراعاة حفظ الأموال وتنميتها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r5.speaker: أبو الفرج الجوزي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r5.claim: Al-Jawzi condemns learned advocates of total divestment as opposing both reason and the law; he says al-Muhasibi and Abu Hamid al-Tusi reinforced that teaching.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r5.anchor: أتعجب من أقوام لهم علم وعقل كيف حثوا على هذا، وأمروا به مع مضادته للشرع والعقل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r6.speaker: المحاسبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r6.claim: Al-Muhasibi recounts that some Companions feared for Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf because of his wealth, while Ka'b defended how he earned, spent, and left it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#10/r6.anchor: لما توفي عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال ناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنما نخاف على عبد الرحمن فيما ترك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r1.claim: The Prophet says the wealthy are few on Judgment Day, except those who give generously in both directions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r1.anchor: الأكثرون هم الأقلون يوم القيامة إلا من قال هكذا وهكذا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r2.speaker: المحاسبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r2.claim: Al-Muhasibi says Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf's lawful earnings delayed his entry with the poor, so he would crawl behind them toward Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r2.anchor: يوقف في عرصة يوم القيامة بسبب ما كسبه من حلال للتعفف وصنائع المعروف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r3.speaker: أبو حامد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r3.claim: Abu Hamid argues that even charitable wealth distracts from remembering God, so an aspirant should retain only necessities and give away every sum that occupies the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r3.anchor: فما بقي له درهم يلتفت إليه قلبه فهو محجوب عن الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r4.speaker: أبو الفرج الجوزي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r4.claim: Al-Jawzi answers that God dignified wealth as human sustenance, prohibited entrusting it to the foolish, and ordered its return when orphans attain sound judgment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r4.anchor: وقد شرفه الله وعظم قدره وأمر بحفظه، إذ جعله قواما للآدمي وما جعل قواما للآدمي الشريف فهو شريف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r5.claim: The Prophet told Sa'd that leaving heirs financially secure is better than leaving them needy and asking people for help.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r5.anchor: إنك أن تذر ورثتك أغنياء خير من أن تذرهم عالة يتكففون الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r6.claim: The Prophet called sound wealth in the hands of a righteous person a good thing.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r7.claim: The Prophet said Abu Bakr's wealth benefited him and prayed for Anas to receive abundant, blessed wealth and children.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r7.anchor: ما نفعني مال كمال أبي بكر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r8.claim: When Ka'b offered to give away all his property as repentance, the Prophet told him to keep some because that was better.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r8.anchor: أمسك عليك بعض مالك فهو خير لك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r9.speaker: أبو الفرج الجوزي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r9.claim: Al-Jawzi acknowledges wealth's temptations but says lawful earnings are necessary; gathering more is judged by intent, and supporting one's family, poor people, and public good can make it better than many devotions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#11/r9.anchor: فإن قصد نفس المفاخرة والمباهاة فبئس المقصود، وإن قصد إعفاف نفسه وعائلته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r1.claim: The Prophet allotted land to al-Zubayr according to how far his horse ran and his whip reached, an example of permitting acquisition.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r1.anchor: أقطع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الزبير حضر فرسه أجرى الفرس حتى قام ثم رمي سوطه، فقال: «أعطوه حيث بلغ سوطه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r2.claim: Desire for increase is natural: Sa'd ibn Ubada prayed for abundance, Joseph's brothers sought an extra camel-load, Shu'ayb offered Moses ten years, and Job gathered golden locusts.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls al-Muhasibi's account of Abu Dharr confronting Ka'b impossible and fabricated; its claimed route through Ibn Lahi'a is unreliable, and Abu Dharr died seven years before Abd al-Rahman.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r3.anchor: والصحيح في التاريخ أن أبا ذر توفي سنة خمس وعشرين، وعبد الرحمن بن عوف توفي سنة اثنتين وثلاثين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r4.claim: The story's content is implausible: the Companions would not condemn wealth lawfully acquired, and it makes no sense that the law would permit and then punish it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r4.anchor: ثم كيف تقول الصحابة: إنا نخاف على عبد الرحمن! أو ليس الإجماع منعقدا على إباحة جمع المال من حله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r5.claim: The crawling report about Abd al-Rahman is weak: its transmitter Ammara ibn Zadhan was criticized by al-Bukhari, Ahmad, Abu Hatim, and al-Daraqutni.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r5.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم الرازي: لا يحتج به، وقال الدارقطني: ضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r6.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says wealth is needed to repay debts and protect one's honor; he left four hundred dinars, while Sufyan al-Thawri called money a weapon in that era.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r6.anchor: لا خير فيمن لا يطلب المال يقضي به دينه ويصون به عرضه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi says soundly intended accumulation of lawful wealth is better than abandoning it; early Muslims praised and gathered it for emergencies and helping the poor, while some chose less to focus on worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#12/r7.anchor: ومتى صح القصد فجمعه أفضل بلا خلاف عند العلماء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#13/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#13/r1.claim: The Prophet's declaration that one killed defending property is a martyr is further evidence that wealth must be protected; fuller discussion is promised in al-Ma'ida.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#13/r1.anchor:
من قتل دون ماله فهو شهيد "
وسيأتي بيانه في «المائدة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#13/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#13/r2.claim: The Prophet says whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr, showing that property deserves protection.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:283#13/r2.anchor: من قتل دون ماله فهو شهيد

RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r1.claim: The passage distinguishes three transaction safeguards: writing with witnesses, taking a pledged security, and relying on trust; the pledge addresses travel when writing or writing tools are unavailable.
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r1.anchor: إعلم أنه تعالى جعل البياعات في هذه الآية على ثلاثة أقسام : بيع بكتاب وشهود

RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r2.claim: The root of safar carries meanings of uncovering or clarification; al-Razi connects it with a book, travel that exposes character, emergence into open country, dawn, and sweeping away dust.
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r2.anchor: تركيب هذه الحروف للظهور والكشف فالسفر هو الكتاب ، لأنه يبين الشيء ويوضحه

RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r3.claim: Rahn derives from permanence and firmness; as a verbal noun it names something deposited as security and functions as a direct object.
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r3.anchor: أصل الرهن من الدوام ، يقال : رهن الشيء إذا دام وثبت

RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r4.claim: A poetic line uses rāhin for pledged sons and illustrates the word’s use as deposited collateral.
RAZI-FULL:v7p104#2/r4.anchor: يراهنني فيرهنني بنيه … وأرهنه بني بما أقول

RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r1.speaker: الأعشى
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r1.claim: Al-Asha uses rahn in a line about refusing to give sons as pledges, illustrating this plural form.
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r1.anchor: آليت لا أعطيه من أبنائنا … رهنا فيفسدهم كمن قد أفسدا

RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r2.speaker: بعيث
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r2.claim: The poet Baith uses al-rahn for pledged property left with a woman, another example of the plural form.
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r2.anchor: بانت سعاد وأمسى دونها عدن … وغلقت عندها من قبلك الرهن

RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r3.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the pattern فعل and فعلى is rare, while the source compares alternations in words such as سقف and نشر.
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج : فعل وفعلى قليل ، وزعم الفراء أن الرهن جمعه رهان

RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r4.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r4.claim: Al-Farra analyzes rahn as a plural of rihan and rihan as a plural of rahn, treating rahn as a plural of a plural.
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r4.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن الرهن جمعه رهان ، ثم الرهان جمعه رهن

RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r5.claim: Another group reverses the proposed relationship, taking rahn as the plural of rahn and rihan as the plural of rahn.
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r5.anchor: ومن الناس من عكس هذا فقال : الرهن جمعه رهن ، والرهن جمعه رهان

RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r6.claim: Al-Razi rejects the disputed plural-of-plural accounts because the proposals cancel each other and Sibawayh does not treat that pattern as regular; he prefers rihan as the straightforward plural of rahn.
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r6.anchor: وأما أن الرهان جمع رهن فهو قياس ظاهر ، مثل نعل ونعال

RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r7.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read فرهان with a damma on both letters, and a further report gives their reading with a still second syllable; Abu Amr distinguishes collateral from horse-racing stakes.
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r7.anchor: قال أبو عمرو : لا أعرف الرهان إلا في الخيل ، فقرأت { فرهان } للفصل بين الرهان في الخيل وبين جمع الرهن

RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r8.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash criticizes Abu Amr reading rahan with a still second syllable because that plural pattern is rare and irregular, though he lists analogies.
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r8.anchor: فقال الأخفش : إنها قبيحة لأن فعلا لا يجمع على فعل إلا قليلا شاذا

RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r9.claim: The clause فرهان مقبوضة is elliptical: it can be an incomplete subject with an omitted predicate, or a predicate with الوثيقة understood as subject.
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r9.anchor: في الآية حذف فإن شئنا جعلناه مبتدأ وأضمرنا الخبر

RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r10.claim: Jurists allow pledges both at home and while traveling; Mujahid limits them to travel, but al-Razi rejects that restriction because travel is the usual context, like fear in the prayer-shortening verse.
RAZI-FULL:v7p105/r10.anchor: وكان مجاهد يذهب إلى أن الرهن لا يجوز إلا في السفر أخذا بظاهر الآية

RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r1.claim: The jurists agree that pledges are valid both at home and on a journey, whether or not a writer is available; the travel condition is customary rather than restrictive.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r1.anchor: احتج من قال بأن رهن المشاع لا يجوز بأن الآية دلت على أن الرهن يجب أن يكون مقبوضا

RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r2.claim: A pledge in jointly owned undivided property is invalid according to the cited argument: a pledge must be received, but an undivided share cannot be physically possessed.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r2.anchor: واعلم أن هذا هو القسم الثالث من البياعات المذكورة في الآية ، وهو بيع الأمانة

RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r3.claim: When the creditor trusts the debtor and takes no written record, witnesses, or pledge, the debtor must honor the trust and repay rather than deny the debt; the verse’s reference to trust means absence of fear of betrayal.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r3.anchor: فقوله { فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا } أي لم يخف خيانته وجحوده

RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r4.claim: An alternative makes the trust-duty address the pledge-holder, who must return the pledge upon repayment, but al-Razi prefers the reading addressed to the debtor.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r4.anchor: وفي الآية قول آخر ، وهو أنه خطاب للمرتهن بأن يؤدي الرهن عند استيفاء المال

RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r5.claim: Al-Razi rejects the claim that this verse abrogates the earlier safeguards: they are recommendations for prudent practice and this verse grants a concession; Ibn ʿAbbas likewise says the debt passage contains no abrogation.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106/r5.anchor: التزام وقوع النسخ من غير دليل يلجىء إليه خطأ ، بل تلك الأوامر محمولة على الإرشاد

RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r1.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r1.claim: Al-Qaffal says that because a trusted debtor may turn out dishonest, God urges anyone who knows the transaction to help preserve the creditor’s right by testifying, whether or not the creditor knows of the testimony.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r1.anchor: ذلك الإنسان إلى أن يسعى في إحياء ذلك الحق

RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r2.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r2.claim: A prophetic report supports Al-Qaffal’s reading: the best witness is one who testifies before being asked.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r2.anchor: خير الشهود من شهد قبل أن يستشهد

RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r3.claim: One interpretation takes concealing testimony to mean denying knowledge of the event, as in the denial concerning Abraham’s family in 2:140.

RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation is withholding testimony when needed; as already stated at 2:282, refusal can defeat a Muslim’s property right and is gravely warned against.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r4.anchor: في كتمان الشهادة والامتناع من أدائها عند الحاجة إلى إقامتها

RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r5.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r5.claim: A report says ʿUmar taught a Bedouin that athīm in the phrase about the tree of Zaqqūm means a wicked person, not an orphan.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r5.anchor: روي أن عمر كان يعلم أعرابيا

RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r6.claim: Al-Kashshāf parses āthim as the predicate of inna and qalbuhu as its nominative agent, equivalent to saying that his heart sins.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r6.anchor: آثم خبر إن وقلبه رفع بآثم على الفاعلية كأنه قيل فإنه يأثم قلبه

RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r7.claim: A reading with qalbahu in the accusative parallels safiha nafsahu in 2:130.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r7.anchor: وقرىء { قلبه } بالفتح كقوله { سفه نفسه }

RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r8.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAblah reads qalbuhu Allāh, explaining the construction as God making the heart sinful.
RAZI-FULL:v7p106#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة { قلبه والله } أي جعله آثما

RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r1.speaker: كثير من المتكلمين
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r1.claim: Many theologians argue that the heart is the acting, knowing, commanded, and prohibited subject; they infer this from God attributing sin to the heart here.
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r1.anchor: إن الفاعل والعارف والمأمور والمنهي هو القلب

RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r2.speaker: من خالف في هذا القول
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r2.claim: Opponents answer that an act can be attributed to a body part because that organ supplies its chief enabling cause, as in saying the eye saw or ear heard.
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r2.anchor: إضافة الفعل إلى جزء من أجزاء البدن إنما يكون لأجل أن أعظم أسباب الإعانة

RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r3.claim: Since bodily acts follow the heart’s motives and inclinations, the sin is attributed to the heart in this verse.
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r3.anchor: أفعال الجوارح تابعة لأفعال القلوب ومتولدة مما يحدث في القلوب من الدواعي والصوارف

RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r4.claim: God’s complete knowledge of actions and inner thoughts warns against concealing testimony: the accountable person knows every deed will be judged and recompensed; the following verse is cited.
RAZI-FULL:v7p107/r4.anchor: إذا علم أنه لا يعزب عن علم الله ضمير قلبه كان خائفا حذرا

STUDYQURAN:2:283/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r1.claim: Not finding a scribe can mean lacking the means to write the contract.
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r1.anchor: And cannot find a scribe can also mean that one does not find the means with which to write the contract down

STUDYQURAN:2:283/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r2.claim: A pledge is collateral given by a debtor to a creditor or by a forward-sale seller to a buyer as security without a written contract and witnesses.
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r2.anchor: collateral property that is given by the debtor to the creditor, or the seller to the buyer in a forward sale

STUDYQURAN:2:283/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r3.claim: The verse allows the parties to trust one another without taking property as a pledge.
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r3.anchor: the verse then leaves open the possibility that one will trust the other party without taking a pledge

STUDYQURAN:2:283/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r4.speaker: Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r4.claim: Some say the trust provision abrogates 2:282’s contract rules; many restrict it to travel and retain written contracts as the ordinary rule.
STUDYQURAN:2:283/r4.anchor: many believe that this provision applies only in the special circumstance of the person being on a journey

TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r1.claim: He prefers the regional reading كاتبا, meaning a person who writes the debt document, because it is the reading in Muslim codices.
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r1.anchor: والقراءة التي لا يجوز غيرها عندنا هي قراءة الأمصار: {ولم تجدوا كاتبا} [البقرة: 283] بمعنى: من يكتب؛

TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r2.speaker: جماعة من المتقدمين
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r2.claim: They read كتابا, meaning no means to produce a written debt record, whether the writer or the writing materials are unavailable.
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ جماعة من المتقدمين: «ولم تجدوا كتابا» بمعنى: ولم يكن لكم إلى

TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r3.claim: When traveling and unable to find a writer to document the deferred debt, creditors may take a pledge in hand as security.
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r3.anchor: وإن كنتم أيها المتداينون في سفر بحيث لا تجدون كاتبا يكتب لكم، ولم يكن لكم إلى اكتتاب كتاب الدين

TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r4.claim: A traveler buying on credit without access to a writer is permitted to take a received pledge; if a writer is available, he may not pledge.
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك، قوله: (وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا فرهن مقبوضة) «فمن كان على سفر

TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r5.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r5.claim: He explains كاتبا as a writer who records the debt and فرهان مقبوضة as a pledge received.
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r5.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع، قوله: {وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا} [البقرة: 283] يقول:

TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r6.claim: He says debts made on credit at home should be recorded and witnessed, while travelers who cannot find a writer take a pledge.
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك، قال: «ما كان من بيع إلى أجل، فأمر الله عز وجل أن يكتب ويشهد عليه وذلك في المقام

TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r7.claim: On the alternative reading, كتاب means the writer, paper, ink, and pen needed for writing.
TAB-FULL:v5p120#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس: «فإن لم تجدوا كتابا» يعني بالكتاب: الكاتب والصحيفة والدواة والقلم

TAB-FULL:v5p123/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r1.claim: He read كتابا, explaining that someone might find paper but no writer.
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه قرأ: «فإن لم تجدوا كتابا» ، قال: «ربما وجد الرجل الصحيفة ولم يجد كاتبا

TAB-FULL:v5p123/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r2.claim: He read كتابا because a writer might be available while paper or ink is not.
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، كان يقرؤها: «فإن لم تجدوا كتابا» ويقول: «ربما وجد الكاتب ولم توجد الصحيفة

TAB-FULL:v5p123/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r3.claim: He glosses كتابا as ink and says a received pledge is required only when traveling and unable to find ink.
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: «وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كتابا» يقول:

TAB-FULL:v5p123/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r4.claim: He read كتابا, explaining that ink might be available while paper is missing.
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r4.anchor: عن شعيب بن الحبحاب، قال: إن أبا العالية كان يقرؤها: «فإن لم تجدوا كتابا» قال أبو العالية: «توجد الدواة

TAB-FULL:v5p123/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r5.claim: Most readers in the Hijaz and Iraq read رهان as the ordinary plural of رهن, like حبال from حبل.
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r5.anchor: قرأ ذلك عامة قراء الحجاز والعراق: {فرهان مقبوضة} [البقرة: 283] بمعنى جماع رهن

TAB-FULL:v5p123/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r6.claim: Other readers use رهن as a plural of رهان or as a plural of a plural; another group treats it as a plural like سقف.
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r6.anchor: وقرأ ذلك جماعة آخرون: (فرهن مقبوضة) على معنى جمع رهان ورهن جمع الجمع

TAB-FULL:v5p123/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r7.claim: Some read رهن with a light h as a plural of رهن, comparing its form to سقف; they acknowledge such plurals are rare.
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r7.anchor: وقرأه آخرون: (فرهن) مخففة الهاء، على معنى جماع رهن، كما تجمع السقف سقفا

TAB-FULL:v5p123/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r8.claim: He prefers رهان because it is the regular, familiar plural pattern for nouns such as حبل and كعب, while the rival plural patterns are rare.
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r8.anchor: والذي هو أولى بالصواب في ذلك قراءة من قرأه: {فرهان مقبوضة} [البقرة: 283] لأن ذلك الجمع المعروف

TAB-FULL:v5p123/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r9.claim: He conjectures that the unusual reading رهن was chosen to avoid confusion with رهان used for horse racing.
TAB-FULL:v5p123/r9.anchor: فيما أظن كذلك مع شذوذه في جمع فعل، أنه وجد الرهان مستعملة في رهان الخيل

TAB-FULL:v5p124/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p124/r1.speaker: قعنب
TAB-FULL:v5p124/r1.claim: The cited line uses الرهن as evidence for the alternative plural form connected with pledges.
TAB-FULL:v5p124/r1.anchor: بانت سعاد وأمسى دونها عدن … وغلقت عندها من قلبك الرهن

TAB-FULL:v5p125/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r1.claim: When a debtor is trusted without collateral, he must fear God and repay rather than deny, delay, or abscond with the debt.
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r1.anchor: ربه في الذي عليه من دين صاحبه أن يجحده، أو يلط دونه، أو يحاول الذهاب به

TAB-FULL:v5p125/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r2.claim: He limits the trust arrangement to travel and says a creditor may neither trust nor take a pledge when a writer is available.
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته} [البقرة: 283] «إنما يعني بذلك في السفر

TAB-FULL:v5p125/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r3.claim: He agrees that when writing and testimony are available, a creditor may not simply rely on the debtor's trustworthiness and omit them.
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r3.anchor: وأما ما قاله من الأمر في الرهن أيضا كذلك مثل الائتمان في أنه ليس لرب الحق الارتهان بماله إذا وجد إلى الكاتب والشهيد سبيلا

TAB-FULL:v5p125/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r4.claim: He rejects restricting pledges to situations without a writer: the Prophet bought food on deferred payment and pledged his armor despite access to writers and witnesses.
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r4.anchor: لصحة الخبر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه اشترى طعاما نساء، ورهن به درعا له

TAB-FULL:v5p125/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r5.claim: If a debt is deferred and a writer and witness are accessible, the parties should document the debt and pledge; omission is allowed only when they lack access.
TAB-FULL:v5p125/r5.anchor: إذا تبايعا برهن، فالواجب عليهما إذا وجدا سبيلا إلى كاتب وشهيد، وكان البيع أو الدين إلى أجل مسمى أن يكتبا ذلك

TAB-FULL:v5p126/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r1.claim: Witnesses must answer when the person for whom they testified calls them to establish that person's right before a judge or ruler.
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r1.anchor: ولكن أجيبوا من شهدتم له إذا دعاكم لإقامة شهادتكم على خصمه على حقه عند الحاكم

TAB-FULL:v5p126/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r2.claim: Concealing testimony makes the witness's heart wicked and guilty of disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r2.anchor: {فإنه آثم قلبه} [البقرة: 283] يقول: فاجر قلبه، مكتسب بكتمانه إياها معصية الله

TAB-FULL:v5p126/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r3.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r3.claim: No one may conceal testimony, even when it is against oneself or one's parents; concealment is a grave sin.
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r3.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع، في قوله: {ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه} [البقرة: 283] «فلا يحل لأحد أن يكتم شهادة

TAB-FULL:v5p126/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r4.claim: He explains the sinful heart as a wicked heart.
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r4.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه} [البقرة: 283] يقول: «فاجر قلبه

TAB-FULL:v5p126/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r5.claim: He counts associating partners with God, false testimony, and concealing testimony among the gravest sins, citing the warning about the concealer's heart.
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " أكبر الكبائر الإشراك بالله؛ لأن الله يقول: {إنه من يشرك بالله فقد حرم الله عليه الجنة

TAB-FULL:v5p126/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r6.claim: A witness should testify wherever summoned and disclose testimony whenever asked about it.
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " إذا كانت عندك شهادة فسألك عنها، فأخبره بها

TAB-FULL:v5p126/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r7.claim: God knows whether people perform or conceal testimony and all their public and private deeds, records them, and recompenses them accordingly.
TAB-FULL:v5p126/r7.anchor: بما تعملون في شهادتكم من إقامتها والقيام بها أو كتمانكم إياها عند حاجة من استشهدكم إليها

TABATABAI:2:282-283/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r1.claim: He defines the key terms: mutual debt, dictation, shortchanging, weariness, causing harm, disobedience, and the two plural forms for pledged collateral.
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r1.anchor: والاملال والاملاء إلقاء الرجل للكاتب ما يكتبه

TABATABAI:2:282-283/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r8.claim: The two verses contain nearly twenty legal rulings, including rules for debt and pledges; detailed legal debate belongs in jurisprudence, so he leaves it aside here.
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r8.anchor: واعلم أن الآيتين تدلان على ما يقرب من عشرين حكما من أصول أحكام الدين والرهن وغيرهما

ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r3.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r3.claim: Some say the exception allowing omission of testimony is ‘if some of you trust others’; the entrusted person must render the debt faithfully.
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r3.anchor: الذي رخص في ترك الإشهاد في قول قوم قوله: (فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته).

ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r4.claim: Rendering the entrusted amount means writing the truth without adding to or subtracting from what is owed; that is justice.
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r4.anchor:
أي يكتب بالحق، لا يكتب لصاحب الدين فضلا على الذي عليه الدين
ولا ينقصه من حقه - فهذا العدل.

ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r4.claim: The readers transmit both رهن and رهان; Abu ʿAmr reads رهن. Some distinguish the latter as horse-race stakes, while others analyze رهن as a plural like سقف; both forms are common.
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r4.anchor:
قرأ الناس " فرهن مقبوضة " و " فرهان مقبوضة "
فأما "رهن" فهي قراءة أبي عمرو،

ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r5.claim: رهن is preferred because it matches the written consonantal text and is sound in meaning and transmitted by readers; رهان is also good and eloquent.
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r5.anchor:
والقراءة على " رهن " أعجب إلي لأنها موافقة
للمصحف، وما وافق المصحف وصح معناه وقرأت به القراء فهو المختار.

ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r6.claim: Arabic uses both رهنت الرهن and أرهنته, and also أرهنت in the sense of pledging or giving a pledge.
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r6.anchor: يقال: رهنت الرهن وأرهنته، وأرهنت أقلهما.

ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r7.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r7.claim: An unnamed poet’s أرهنتهم مالكا illustrates the verb أرهنت.
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r7.anchor:
قال الشاعر في أرهنت:
فلما خشيت أظافيرهم. . . نجوت وأرهنتهم مالكا

ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r8.speaker: غير واحد
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r8.claim: Several transmitters cite poetry with يراهنني فيرهنني to illustrate رهنت and the related pledging forms.
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r8.anchor:
وقال في رهنت: أنشده غير واحد:
فهل من كاهن أو ذي إله. . . إذا ما حان من ربي قفول
يراهنني فيرهنني بنيه. . . وأرهنه بني بما أقول

TABRISI:2:283#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
TABRISI:2:283#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read رهن as faʿl; the other readers read رهٰان on the faʿāl pattern.
TABRISI:2:283#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو فرهن على وزن فعل والباقون فرهان على وزن فعال

TABRISI:2:283#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#2/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:2:283#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī says رهن began as a verbal noun, became a noun by transfer, and is pluralized on both فعْل and فعال patterns; the cited verse attests the form.
TABRISI:2:283#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: الرهن مصدر ولما نقل فسمي به كسر

TABRISI:2:283#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283#2/r3.claim: The root رهن means placing property as security; a pledge may also be called a mortgage, with related alternative forms and expressions for advancing or maintaining food.
TABRISI:2:283#2/r3.anchor: يقال رهنت عند الرجل رهنا ورهنته رهنا وأنا أرهنه

TABRISI:2:283#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#2/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
TABRISI:2:283#2/r4.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says the reading أرهنتهم مالكا in Ibn Hammām's verse is mistaken; the correct wording is وأرهنهم مالكا.
TABRISI:2:283#2/r4.anchor: قال الأصمعي من روي بيت ابن همام

TABRISI:2:283#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283#2/r5.claim: The Prophetic rule لا يغلق الرهن invalidates a condition that if the borrower does not redeem by a set date the collateral becomes the creditor's property.
TABRISI:2:283#2/r5.anchor: " لا يغلق الرهن " فمعناه أن يقول الراهن

TABRISI:2:283#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283#2/r6.claim: When debtors travel without a scribe or witnesses, a received pledge serves as security and is valid only upon possession, by consensus.
TABRISI:2:283#2/r6.anchor: والقبض شرط في صحة الرهن فإن لم يقبض لم ينعقد الرهن بالاجماع

TABRISI:2:283#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283#2/r7.claim: If the creditor trusts the debtor without a written or pledged security, the debtor must fully repay at maturity without denial or delay.
TABRISI:2:283#2/r7.anchor: بأن لا يجحد حقه ولا يبخس منه شيئا ويؤديه إليه وافيا

TABRISI:2:283#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283#2/r8.claim: The order not to conceal testimony addresses witnesses after they have borne it; intentional concealment by one who knows the fact and can testify without harm makes the heart sinful.
TABRISI:2:283#2/r8.anchor: يعني بعد تحملها وهو خطاب للشهود ونهي لهم عن كتمان الشهادة

TABRISI:2:283#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283#2/r9.claim: Sin is assigned to the heart because the decision to conceal is made there, and this wording intensifies blame; the verse on faith in hearts provides a parallel.
TABRISI:2:283#2/r9.anchor: لأن اكتساب الإثم بكتمان الشهادة يقع بالقلب لأن العزم على الكتمان إنما يقع بالقلب

TABRISI:2:283#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283#3/r1.claim: God knows what people conceal; a report from the Prophet says a false witness leaves the judge only after taking his seat in Hell, as does one who hides testimony.
TABRISI:2:283#3/r1.anchor: لا ينقضي كلام شاهد زور من بين يدي الحاكم حتى يتبوأ مقعده من النار

TABRISI:2:283#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283#3/r2.claim: The clause permitting trust between the parties shows that writing and witnesses in debt transactions are safeguards, not obligations.
TABRISI:2:283#3/r2.anchor: دلالة على أن الاشهاد والكتابة في المداينة ليسا بواجبين

TABRISI:2:283#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283#3/r3.claim: The two verses show God's care in teaching people what they need for worldly and religious life, offering insight to the reflective.
TABRISI:2:283#3/r3.anchor: وتضمنت هذه الآية وما قبلها من بدائع لطف الله تعالى ونظره لعباده

THALABI:v2p297#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو العالية ومجاهد
THALABI:v2p297#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aliyya, and Mujahid read كِتابا, understanding it as writing materials: a writer could be present while ink or paper was unavailable.
THALABI:v2p297#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عباس وأبو العالية ومجاهد: كتابا، وقالوا: ربما وجد الكاتب ولم يجد المداد ولا الصحيفة،

THALABI:v2p297#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v2p297#2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reads كُتّابا as the plural of writer.
THALABI:v2p297#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك: كتابا على جمع الكاتب.

THALABI:v2p297#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p297#2/r3.claim: The majority reads كاتبا in the singular, which best fits the written muṣḥaf.
THALABI:v2p297#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: كاتبا على الواحد وهو الأنسب مع المصحف.

THALABI:v2p297#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وإبراهيم وزر بن حبيش ومجاهد وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
THALABI:v2p297#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibrahim, Zirr, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read the pledge noun as رُهُن with both letters vowelled.
THALABI:v2p297#2/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن عباس وإبراهيم وزر بن حبيش ومجاهد وابن كثير وأبو عمرو: فرهن بضم الراء والهاء.

THALABI:v2p297#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة والمنهال وعبد الوارث
THALABI:v2p297#2/r5.claim: Ikrima, al-Minhal, and Abd al-Warith read رُهْن with a silent hāʾ.
THALABI:v2p297#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة والمنهال وعبد الوارث: فرهن بضم الراء وجزم الهاء،

THALABI:v2p297#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297#2/r6.speaker: الفراء والكسائي
THALABI:v2p297#2/r6.claim: Al-Farra and al-Kisaʾi analyze رهان as a plural of رهن, itself a plural of the form رهان.
THALABI:v2p297#2/r6.anchor: والرهن جمع الرهان: جمع الجمع، قاله الفراء والكسائي.

THALABI:v2p297#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297#2/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v2p297#2/r7.claim: Abu Ubayd and other grammarians instead analyze رهان as a direct plural of رهن and list rare nouns with a similar plural pattern.
THALABI:v2p297#2/r7.anchor: وقال غيرهما وأبو عبيدة: هو جمع الرهن. قالوا: ولم نجد فعلا يجمع على فعل

THALABI:v2p297#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p297#2/r8.claim: The segment cites verse and poetic evidence for the noun pattern, but the first cited poem is textually incomplete in the source.
THALABI:v2p297#2/r8.anchor: قال الأخطل وعمرو بن أبي عوف: [ ... ] به حتى يغادره العقبان والنسر.

THALABI:v2p298/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p298/r1.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v2p298/r1.claim: Al-Farra cites a line about throats and a ridge to attest a form related to the pledge reading.
THALABI:v2p298/r1.anchor: حتى إذا بلت حلاقيم الحلق … أهوى لأدنى فقرة على شفق

THALABI:v2p298/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p298/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
THALABI:v2p298/r2.claim: Abu Amr says he reads فرهن to distinguish the pledge word from رهان used for horse wagers; Qanʿab's poem uses الرهن for love's hold.
THALABI:v2p298/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: وإنما قرأنا (فرهن) ليكون قرفا [بينها وبين] رهان الخيل،

THALABI:v2p298/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p298/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p298/r3.claim: Vowelled and unvowelled forms of the pledge noun are dialect variants, like the cited paired forms.
THALABI:v2p298/r3.anchor: والتخفيف والتثقيل في الرهن لغتان مثل كتب وكتب ورسل ورسل

THALABI:v2p298/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p298/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p298/r4.claim: When traveling without a scribe, take collateral from the debtor to secure the debt.
THALABI:v2p298/r4.anchor: فارتهنوا ممن تداينونه رهونا ليكون وثيقة لكم بأموالكم.

THALABI:v2p298/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p298/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p298/r5.claim: Jurists agree that a pledge is not legally complete until possession is transferred.
THALABI:v2p298/r5.anchor: وأجمعوا: إن الرهن لا يصح إلا بالقبض،

THALABI:v2p298/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p298/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v2p298/r6.claim: Mujahid confines pledging to travel when no writer is available, while other jurists allow it in all circumstances.
THALABI:v2p298/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ليس الرهن إلا في السفر عند عدم الكاتب. وأجاز غيره في جميع الأحوال.

THALABI:v2p298/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p298/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p298/r7.claim: The Prophet once pledged his armor to a Jewish creditor.
THALABI:v2p298/r7.anchor: ورهن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم درعه عند يهودي

THALABI:v2p298/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p298/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p298/r8.claim: If the debtor is trusted and the creditor waives collateral out of confidence, the debtor must return the entrusted debt and fear God in payment.
THALABI:v2p298/r8.anchor: فإن كان الذي عليه الحق أمينا عند صاحب الحق فلم يرتهن منه شيئا لثقته

THALABI:v2p298/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p298/r9.speaker: السلمي
THALABI:v2p298/r9.claim: Al-Sulami reads the command against concealing testimony in the third person, and does the same for يعملون.
THALABI:v2p298/r9.anchor: ثم رجع إلى خطاب الشهود فقال: ولا تكتموا الشهادة. إذا دعيتم إلى إقامتها، وقرأ السلمي: ولا يكتموا بالياء ومثله يعملون.

THALABI:v2p298/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p298/r10.speaker: إبراهيم بن أبي عيلة
THALABI:v2p298/r10.claim: Ibrahim ibn Abi Aylah reads أثم قلبه on the أفعل pattern, meaning that the person has made his heart sinful.
THALABI:v2p298/r10.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم بن أبي عيلة: فإنه أثم قلبه على وزن أفعل

THALABI:v2p298/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p298/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p298/r11.claim: A Prophetic report says concealing testimony when summoned is like giving false testimony.
THALABI:v2p298/r11.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من كتم الشهادة إذا دعي

ASAD-NOTES:2:283#n276/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:283#n276/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:283#n276/r1.claim: The ban on concealing testimony covers transaction witnesses and a debtor who accepted a trust-based loan without writing or witnesses and later denies the debt.
ASAD-NOTES:2:283#n276/r1.anchor: a debtor who has been given a loan on trust - without a written agreement and without witnesses

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r5.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r5.claim: Others say writing, witnesses, or collateral were initially obligatory but were abrogated by the trust clause in 2:283, which permits leaving documentation when the parties trust each other.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: كانت الكتابة والإشهاد أو الرهن فرضا، ثم نسخ ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r6.claim: Asked by al-Taymī, al-Ḥasan said the parties may witness or omit witnesses, citing the clause that some may trust others.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r6.anchor: قال التيمي: سألت الحسن عنها فقال: إن شاء أشهد، وإن شاء لم يشهد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says scholars in the Ḥijāz and Iraq agree that sale witnesses are not mandatory and that buyers can choose; they treat the following trust clause as abrogating the obligation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: والعلماء اليوم من أهل الحجاز وأهل العراق وغيرهم على هذا القول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r1.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r1.claim: Language scholars connect safar, travel, with revealing character; related forms include a book that makes things clear, dawn appearing, a woman uncovering her face, reconciling parties by revealing feelings, and sweeping away.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r1.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: سمي السفر سفرا لأنه يسفر عن أخلاق الرجال (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r2.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r2.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī defines safar as the brightening of dawn; al-Akhṭal’s line describes staying up until the light opens the way.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r3.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r3.claim: Al-Azharī explains that a traveler reveals what was hidden by emerging into open country; safar also names the remaining daylight after sunset, illustrated by a weather saying about Sirius.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r3.anchor: وقال الأزهري: وسمي المسافر مسافرا لكشفه قناع الكن عن وجهه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r4.claim: Sāfira and safar are plurals of sāfir, and misfar describes a man strong enough for travel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p510/r4.anchor: والسافرة والسفر: جمع سافر (¬2)، ورجل مسفر: قوي على السفر (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r1.claim: Rahn is the verbal noun of pledging something with someone; the source cites poetry illustrating the noun and verb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r1.anchor: الرهن: مصدر رهنت عند الرجل رهنا فأنا أرهنه: إذا وضعته عنده.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says arhan can mean rahana and cites Ibn Hammām al-Salūlī; al-Aṣmaʿī rejects that reading, preferring arhanahum as a circumstantial clause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r2.anchor: وأرهنت بمعنى رهنت، لغة عند الفراء، واحتج ببيت ابن همام السلولي:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r3.claim: The pledged object is called rahn after a verbal noun shifts into a noun; in this use its case is that of a direct object, not a cognate accusative.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r3.anchor: ولما نقل فسمي به جمع كما تجمع الأسماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r4.claim: As a noun, rahn forms plurals on fuʿul and fiʿāl; the language did not record an afʿul plural, apparently because the frequent plural sufficed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r4.anchor: فرهن جمع على بناءين من أبنية الجموع وهو فعل وفعال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r5.claim: Poetic and lexical evidence supports fuʿul plurals such as ruhun, alongside comparable plural doublets and varied forms quoted from al-Akhfash.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r5.anchor: فرهن: جمع رهن، ثم تخفف العين كما تخفف في رسل وكتب، ونحو ذلك،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ proposes that ruhan is a plural of rihān, itself a plural of rahn, analogous to thamar as a plural of thimār and jamāʾil from jimāl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p511/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء: الرهن: جمع رهان، جمع الجمع،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads ruhun to distinguish pledged collateral from horse-betting: ruhun is common for pledges, while rihān is common for horse races.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r1.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: وإنما قرأت: (فرهن) للفصل بين الرهان في الخيل وبين جمع رهن في غيرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj chooses the ruhun reading because it matches the codex and has a sound meaning, following the rule that a reading meeting those conditions is preferred.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r2.anchor: واختار الزجاج هذه القراءة، قال: لأنها موافقة للمصحف،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r3.claim: The common rihān reading is the regular plural of rahn, like niʿāl from naʿl; although some allow it as a plural of the plural, the author invokes Sibawayh’s caution against assuming that process without evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r3.anchor: وأما قراءة العامة {فرهان مقبوضة} (¬7) فإنها القياس في جمع رهن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r4.claim: Rahn derives from something that remains firmly fixed; the cited poetry shows the sense of enduring stability.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p514/r4.anchor: فأما اشتقاق الرهن في اللغة، فأصله: من قولهم: رهن الشيء: إذا دام وثبت،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r1.speaker: اللحياني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r1.claim: Al-Liḥyānī’s forms for trusting someone lead to the verse’s sense: some parties do not fear the other’s betrayal or denial of the debt; the passage cites 8:11 and 12:64.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r1.anchor: قال اللحياني: أمن فلان غيره على الشيء يأمن أمنا وأمنة وأمنة (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r2.claim: Ūtumin is the passive of iftaʿala from amāna; the text gives related active, passive, and participial forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r2.anchor: اؤتمن: افتعل، من الأمانة، يقال: أمنته وايتمنته،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the heart has sinned and acted wickedly when testimony is concealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد قد أثم قلبه وفجر (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r4.claim: Exegetes note that the threat for concealing testimony specifies sin of the heart; they say it may cause the heart to be transformed into a hypocrite’s heart and sealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون: ذكر الله تعالى على كتمان الشهادة نوعا من الوعيد لم يذكره في سائر الكبائر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r5.speaker: أبو موسى عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r5.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet saying that one who conceals testimony when summoned is like one who gave false testimony.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p517/r5.anchor: وروى أبو موسى عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:283-286/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:283-286/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:283-286/r1.claim: When traveling without a scribe, take a received pledge as security; if parties trust one another, the entrusted debtor must repay and fear God.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:283-286/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:283-286/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:283-286/r2.claim: Do not conceal testimony when called to give it; whoever conceals it is sinful in heart.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:283-286/r2.anchor: { ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم } فاجر { قلبه }

ELMALILI:2:283/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r1.claim: A pledge is the recourse when traveling and no scribe is available, but these conditions concern resort to collateral, not its validity or permissibility.
ELMALILI:2:283/r1.anchor: bu şartlar rehnin sıhhat ve cevâzının değil, tevsik için ta‘ayyününün şartıdır.

ELMALILI:2:283/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r2.claim: The verse’s travel-and-no-scribe condition cannot be inverted to forbid pledges when one is resident or a scribe is available; the lack of a scribe makes writing impossible.
ELMALILI:2:283/r2.anchor: bu şartın “seferde olmaz veya kâtib bulursanız rehin alamazsınız” diye mefhûm-ı muhâlifi muteber değildir.

ELMALILI:2:283/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r3.claim: Travel is the customary or usual cause of lacking a scribe, not a restrictive condition; the same rule applies to another excuse that prevents finding a scribe while resident.
ELMALILI:2:283/r3.anchor: Sefer bunun sebeb-i âdî ve ekserîsidir. Ta‘bîr-i âharla ihtirâzî değil, kayd-ı vukū‘îdir.

ELMALILI:2:283/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r4.claim: A pledge is permissible while resident too, as shown by the Prophet pledging his coat of mail in a settled state.
ELMALILI:2:283/r4.anchor: Hazarda rehnin cevâzı fi‘l-i nebevî ile de sâbittir. Çünkü Resûlullah hâl-i hazarda zırhlı gömleğini rehnetmiştir.

ELMALILI:2:283/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r5.claim: When writing can secure a debt, requesting a pledge between believers is permissible but not recommended unless there is an excuse.
ELMALILI:2:283/r5.anchor: senet ve kitabet ile tevsik mümkin oldukça mü’minler beynindeki müdâyenâtta rehin talep etmek câiz olsa da mendub olmayacaktır

ELMALILI:2:283/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r6.claim: Taking possession is required to complete a pledge; an unpossessed pledge gives no security, and an undivided fractional share cannot properly be pledged.
ELMALILI:2:283/r6.anchor: rehnin tamam olması için kabz şarttır, makbuz olmayan rehin bir tevsik ifade etmez.

ELMALILI:2:283/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r7.claim: Writing, witnessing, and pledging are the three means of securing debts and transactions; faith and piety should encourage these protections of people’s rights and lawful wealth.
ELMALILI:2:283/r7.anchor: müdâyenât ve mu‘âmelâtta üç nevi tevsik vardır: Kitabet, işhâd, rehin.

ELMALILI:2:283/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r8.claim: Securing lawful wealth enables lawful earning and spending in God’s path and helps avoid usury and similar sins so that piety can continue.
ELMALILI:2:283/r8.anchor: mâl-i helâli muhafaza ve helâk ü zayâ‘dan sıyânet ederek tarîk-i meşrû‘ile kesb ü istihsâle sa‘y eylemelidir

ELMALILI:2:283/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r9.claim: The strongest assurance for human rights is obedience to God through faith and piety; without it, secondary safeguards have limited benefit.
ELMALILI:2:283/r9.anchor: hukūk-ı beşer için bu meyanda en büyük te’mînât Hak teâlâ’ya inkıyad ile ahkâmına i‘tisâm bahş eden hiss-i dîn ü takvâdadır.

ELMALILI:2:283/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r10.claim: It is permissible for parties to dispense with all three securities and rely wholly on mutual trust; the trusted debtor must repay the trust.
ELMALILI:2:283/r10.anchor: bazınız bazınıza, bazı dâyinler bazı medyunlara tamamen emniyet eder, rehin almaz

ELMALILI:2:283/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r11.claim: Permission to rely on trust shows that writing, witnessing, and pledging are recommendations rather than obligations; otherwise this permission would abrogate the prior commands.

ELMALILI:2:283/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r12.speaker: Hasan, Şa‘bî, Hakem b. Uteybe
ELMALILI:2:283/r12.claim: Hasan, al-Shaʿbi, and al-Hakam b. Utayba are among exegetes who say this verse abrogates the earlier instructions.
ELMALILI:2:283/r12.anchor: mahmul olursa o vücûbun bununla mensuh olmasını iktizâ edecektir. Fi’l-hakīka Hasan, Şa‘bî,

ELMALILI:2:283/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas explicitly says the debt verse is not abrogated but remains decisive; with no proof that this verse came later, most exegetes agree there is no abrogation.
ELMALILI:2:283/r13.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretleri âyet-i müdâyenede nesih yoktur, muhkemdir diye tasrih ettiği

ELMALILI:2:283/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r14.claim: Most exegetes treat permission to rely on trust as evidence that the securities are recommended; ʿAta, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Nakhaʿi instead make the pledge recommended while treating feasible writing and witnessing as obligatory.
ELMALILI:2:283/r14.anchor: ekserîsi işbu cevâz-ı emniyetin nâsih değil, karîne-i nedb olduğuna; Atâ, İbn Cüreyc, Nehaî gibi bazıları da

ELMALILI:2:283/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r15.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi’s account in Ahkam al-Qur’an says the juristic position is recommendation.
ELMALILI:2:283/r15.anchor: Ahkâm-ı Kur’ân’da Ebû Bekir Râzî’nin beyânına nazaran fıkıh nedb üzerindedir.

ELMALILI:2:283/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r16.claim: Whatever the status of the safeguards, the person entrusted with property is obligated to discharge the trust fully and must fear God rather than misuse the trust.
ELMALILI:2:283/r16.anchor: emniyet edilen şahıs emaneti bihakkın edâ etmek farz olduğunu bilsin

ELMALILI:2:283/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r17.claim: Witnesses must neither refuse to testify when needed nor conceal known truth; debtors likewise must not deny a debt they know and have witnessed.
ELMALILI:2:283/r17.anchor: ey şâhidler lede’l-hâce edâ-yı şehadetten hem imtinâ‘etmeyiniz, hem de görüp bildiğiniz hakk u hakikati gizlemeyiniz.

ELMALILI:2:283/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r18.claim: Concealing testimony is a grave inward sin of the heart, the locus of faith, and approaches unbelief or lack of creed.
ELMALILI:2:283/r18.anchor: Ketm-i şehadet günahı öyle zâhirî ve hâricî bir uzvun günahı değil, bizzat mahall-i iman olan kalb ve nefsin bir günahıdır.

ELMALILI:2:283/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r19.claim: Ibn Abbas counts associating partners with God, false testimony, and concealing testimony among the greatest major sins.
ELMALILI:2:283/r19.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan mervîdir ki “ekber-i kebâir Allah’a şirk, yalancı şâhidlik ve ketm-i şehâdettir”

ELMALILI:2:283/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:283/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:283/r20.claim: God knows every hidden and manifest act, including giving or concealing testimony, and will punish accordingly.
ELMALILI:2:283/r20.anchor: Allah ise şehadet veya ketm-i şehadet gibi gizli açık, zâhir veya bâtında her ne yaparsanız tamamıyla bilir. Sırası gelince cezasını verir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r1.claim: Collateral is a material asset taken from the debtor and convertible to payment; Islam forbids using a human being as collateral, despite pre-Islamic practices that sometimes pledged children.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r1.anchor: İslâm’da rehin konusunun insan olması câiz değildir
