KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r2.claim: When travel makes a scribe hard to find, a suitable pledge can replace writing; the Prophet's practice shows pledges are allowed outside travel as well.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r2.anchor: Rehin almanın câiz olması yolculuk haline özgü de değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r3.speaker: Hanefî ve Şâfiîler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r3.claim: Hanafis and Shafiis say a pledge contract is invalid if the collateral has not been taken out of the debtor's control; Malik says it is valid but binding only upon delivery, and the debtor can be compelled to deliver it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r3.anchor: Hanefî ve Şâfiîler’e göre akid sahih olmaz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r4.claim: A creditor may not benefit from property pledged as security for a debt.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r4.anchor: Borca karşı teminat olarak alınan rehinden alacaklının istifade etmesi câiz değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r5.claim: Among jurists who consider writing, dictation, and witnesses obligatory, some take the mutual-trust clause to lift that obligation, while others limit pledges as a substitute to travel; those who see security as recommended view the clause as reinforcing that advice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r5.anchor: Yazma, yazdırma, şahit tutmanın farz olduğunu söyleyenlerin bir kısmına göre âyetin bu bölümü farz olma hükmünü kaldırmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r6.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur's wider reading, which the author endorses, extends fidelity to trust across all debt relations; without trust and responsibility, parties can wrong one another even when security exists.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r6.anchor: İbn Âşûr’un da işaret ettiği üzere güvene karşı ihanet etmemeyi, emaneti yerine getirmeyi bütün borç ilişkilerine yaymak daha doğrudur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r7.claim: Those who know relevant testimony may not conceal it; they should come forward even if not asked, while hadiths criticizing unsolicited testimony are understood as concerning God's rights or false testimony.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r7.anchor: tanık olanların bildiklerini gizlemeleri câiz değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r8.claim: Concealing testimony is a sin of the mind and will rather than an outward bodily act, which explains calling the heart sinful.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:283/r8.anchor: Şahitliği gizlemek, bildiğini söylememek dışa vuran vücut hareketiyle değil

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read رهن without alif, with transmitters differing over a silent or vocalized hāʾ; Nafi, Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Kisai read رهان with alif and kasra on rāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r1.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي فرهان بألف مكسورة الراء

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r2.claim: Abu Zayd says رهن is something deposited as security and ارتهن is taking it; he also records رهن/أرهن for continuing or maintaining something, with poetry as evidence.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r2.anchor: فقد فسروا الرهن بالإثبات والإدامة، فمن ثم يبطل الرهن إذا خرج من يد المرتهن

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r3.claim: A pledge is a nominal verbal noun like كتابه in 66:12; once a verbal noun becomes a lexical name, it no longer governs objects as a verb would.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p442/r3.anchor: والرهن الذي يمسكه المرتهن توثقة لاستيفاء ماله من الراهن: اسم مصدر كما كان الكتاب كذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r1.claim: Although analogies from plural patterns such as طرقات could support another broken plural, the author says stopping at the attested form is preferable because singular and plural patterns do not license one another without evidence.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r1.anchor: هذا قياس، التوقف عنه نراه أولى، وقد ذهب إليه ناس

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r2.speaker: أحمد بن موسى
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r2.claim: Ahmad ibn Musa's entry for Hamza and Asim's reading of الذي اؤتمن is marked as a mistake; the other readers use a hamza preceded by a kasra and left silent.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r3.speaker: أحمد بن موسى
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r3.claim: Ahmad says the reported pronunciation with ḍamma-tinged hamza is wrong; the only correct form leaves the hamza silent.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r3.anchor: وهذا هو الصواب الذي لا يجوز غيره

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r4.claim: Ishmām cannot put a vowel on the hamza itself, since the first radical of افتعل is always silent; nor can a preceding vowel be transferred forward, as transfer operates toward the preceding consonant.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p449/r4.anchor: الفاء من افتعل ساكنة في جميع الكلام صحيحه ومعتله

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104#2/r1.claim: The reading رُهُن is explained as a plural of رهن, while رِهان is also a plural of رهن; the author notes that رهن and سقف are rare plurals on this pattern.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104#2/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن ضم أنه جمع رهنا رهانا وجمع رهانا رهنا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r4.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو، نافع، عاصم، حمزة، الكسائي، ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r4.claim: The readers vary in فرهان: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr use the form without alif, with differing reports on hāʾ voweling; Nafi, Asim, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Ibn Amir read رهان with kasra and alif.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وابن عامر ﴿ فرهان ﴾ بكسر الراء والألف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r1.speaker: حمزة، عاصم عن يحيى بن آدم عن أبي بكر، حفص
IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r1.claim: These transmissions read الذي اؤتمن with a raised, rounded hamza; Abu Bakr says that notation is not valid Arabic, and another Hamza transmission is likewise called erroneous unless the hamza is quiescent.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة وعاصم في رواية يحيى بن آدم عن أبي بكر وحفص عنه ﴿ الذي اؤتمن ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r2.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r2.claim: The author declares the quiescent hamza reading the only correct form and rejects the rounded or vowel-signaled hamza variants.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r2.anchor: وهذا خطأ لا يجوز إلا تسكين الهمزة

QIRAAT-ER:2:283:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:283:11#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:283:11#1/r1.claim: Ruhun and rihān are both canonical plurals of rahn: the former is broken and the latter sound.
QIRAAT-ER:2:283:11#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant: ruhun (plural of rahn) instead of rihān — both are valid plurals

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#2/r1.speaker: الشعبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#2/r1.claim: Al-Sha‘bi says that when the parties trust one another, they may dispense with both writing and testimony.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p111#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن شبرمة عن الشعبي في قوله تعالى ﴿ فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا ﴾ قال لا بأس به إذا أمنته ألا تكتب ولا تشهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r1.speaker: مجاهد، الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r1.claim: They infer that pledges and trust apply only in travel and reject pledges at home; the majority allow pledges at home and with a scribe. Travel represents an excuse, and the Prophet's armor pledged at home shows the condition is not restrictive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r1.anchor: وقد ذهب مجاهد، والضحاك: إلى أن الرهن والائتمان إنما هو في السفر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r2.claim: Travel represents any excuse that prevents writing or witnessing, including busy periods and nighttime.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r2.anchor: ونبه بالسفر على كل عذر، وقد يتعذر الكاتب في الحضر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r3.speaker: أبي، مجاهد، أبو العالية، ابن عباس، الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r3.claim: Some read kātiban as kutuban, a verbal noun or plural of writer; Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take it as plural for multiple cases, and Abū al-ʿĀliya also reads kutuban as plural of kitāb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبي، ومجاهد، وأبو العالية: كتابا على أنه مصدر، أو جمع كاتب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r4.claim: Readers differ among farhān, ruhun, and ruhn; grammarians debate plural formation, Abū ʿAmr prefers the reduced dialect form, and Yūnus says rihān is Arabic but common for horses; al-Aʿshā's verse witnesses rahn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فرهان، جمع رهن نحو: كعب وكعاب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء، الأعشى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr says rihān is used for horses; al-Aʿshā's poem gives an example of rahn as the plural for pledges.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p742/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: لا أعرف الرهان إلا في الخيل لا غير،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r1.claim: “Held in possession” requires taking; all accept possession by creditor or agent, while the majority accept a neutral custodian and ʿAṭāʾ, Qatāda, al-Ḥakam, and Ibn Abī Laylā do not.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r1.anchor: والظاهر من قوله: مقبوضة، اشتراط القبض. وأجمع الناس على صحة قبض المرتهن،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r2.speaker: الشافعي، أبو حنيفة، المالكية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r2.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfa make possession a condition of validity; Mālik makes the contract binding before delivery and compels transfer, possession being required for full benefit. All agree the pledge is incomplete without it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r2.anchor: فالظاهر من الآية أنه لا يصح إلا بالقبض، وبه قال الشافعي وأبو حنيفة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r3.speaker: مالك، أبو حنيفة، الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r3.claim: Mālik says return to the pledgor voids the pledge; Abū Ḥanīfa preserves it if returned as loan or deposit; al-Shāfiʿī voids it whenever returned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r3.anchor: واختلفوا في استمراره، فقال مالك: إذا رده بعارية أو غيرها بطل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r4.speaker: الجمهور، المالكية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r4.claim: The majority require valuable, saleable, deliverable property and reject a debt as collateral and uncertain items; Mālik permits a debt and uncertain property such as runaway slave, stray camel, fetus, fish in water, or unripe fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r4.anchor: فقال الجمهور: لا يجوز رهن ما في الذمة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r5.speaker: مالك، الشافعي، أبو حنيفة، الحسن بن صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r5.claim: Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī permit an undivided share whether divisible or not; Abū Ḥanīfa rejects it altogether; al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ permits it only if indivisible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r5.anchor: واختلفوا في رهن المشاع، فقال مالك، والشافعي: يصح فيما يقسم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p743/r6.claim: “On a journey” means “while travelling”; wa-lam tajidū has several syntactic attachments, and farhān is predicate of an omitted subject: “the security is a pledge.”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r1.claim: If a creditor trusts the debtor and advances property without writing, witnesses, or pledge, the debtor must repay it without evasion or delay; jurists agree repayment is obligatory and enforceable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r1.anchor: أي: إن وثق رب الدين بأمانة الغريم، فدفع إليه ماله بغير كتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r2.speaker: أبي، السجاوندي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r2.claim: Ubay reads fa-in ūmina in passive form, “if people trust him”; al-Sajāwandī reports fa-in iʾtamana as trust without a written instrument or pledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبي: فإن أومن، رباعيا مبنيا للمفعول،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r3.claim: The pronoun in “his trust” may refer to creditor or debtor; amāna may mean the owed thing or act of trust, with “debt” understood elliptically.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r3.anchor: والضمير في: أمانته، يحتمل أن يعود إلى رب الدين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r4.claim: Reported readings alter the hamza of alladhī uʾtumina by vowel indication, ishām, or substitution with yāʾ; Abū Ḥayyān questions some notations and explains its original two hamzas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن، وورش بإبدال الهمزة ياء، كما أبدلت في بئر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r5.speaker: عاصم، الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r5.claim: A rare ʿĀṣim reading assimilates the tāʾ substituted for hamza; al-Zamakhsharī rejects it, though other grammarians report it as a poor dialect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p744/r5.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في شاذه: اللذتمن، بإدغام التاء المبدلة من الهمزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r1.claim: The debtor must fear God's punishment in repaying entrusted property; “God, his Lord” stresses piety at acknowledgment and repayment, echoing 2:282.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r1.anchor: وليتق الله ربه أي عذاب الله في أداء ما ائتمنه رب المال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r2.claim: Concealing testimony is forbidden where a right may be lost; Ibn ʿAbbās says testify when summoned and report directly to the person concerned, not merely to an official.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r2.anchor: ولا تكتموا الشهادة هذا نهي تحريم، ألا ترى إلى الوعيد لمن كتمها؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r3.speaker: السلمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r3.claim: Al-Sulamī reads the prohibition in third-person plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r3.anchor: وقرأ السلمي: ولا يكتموا، بالياء على الغيبة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r4.claim: Concealment means withholding testimony; sin is assigned to the heart because testimony is knowledge held there, using part for whole and emphasizing the heart as source of outward action; a prophetic hadith compares it to the body's governing morsel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r4.anchor: ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه كتم الشهادة هو إخفاؤها بالامتناع من أدائها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r5.claim: The majority parse āthim as an active participle with qalbuhu its raised subject; al-Zamakhsharī offers a fronted predicate, while Ibn ʿAṭiyya's analysis is rejected by Basran grammarians except on Abū al-Ḥasan's approach.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p745/r5.anchor: وقراءة الجمهور: آثم، اسم فاعل من: أثم قلبه، و: قلبه، مرفوع به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r1.speaker: ابن عطية، ابن أبي عبلة، مكي، الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests qalbuhu is partitive apposition; Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads it accusative, parsed by Makkī as explanatory despite definiteness. Other parses compare it with object-like constructions or apposition to inna; a variant has athama qalbahu, “he made his heart sinful.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r1.anchor: وقرأ قوم: قلبه، بالنصب، ونسبها ابن عطية إلى ابن أبي عبلة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān identifies the first grammatical analysis as preferred.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r3.claim: God's knowledge covers all acts, including concealment and proper delivery of testimony; it is a severe threat because knowledge entails recompense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r3.anchor: وفي الجملة توعد شديد لكاتم الشهادة، لأن علمه بها يترتب عليه المجازاة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r4.claim: The passage uses contrasting paronomasia in debt/indebtedness, writer/writing, and entrustment/trust.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r4.anchor: التجنيس المغاير في قوله: إذا تداينتم بدين، وفي قوله: وليكتب بينكم كاتب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r1.claim: It uses matching paronomasia in “do not conceal testimony” and “whoever conceals it.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r1.anchor: والتجنيس الممائل في قوله: ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r4.claim: The closing catalogue identifies ellipsis and explains implied subjects and objects in writing, dictation, testimony, repayment, and not concealing testimony.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r4.anchor: والحذف في قوله: يا أيها الذين آمنوا، حذف متعلق الإيمان.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r1.claim: Being upon a journey is a dependent metaphor for being firmly established in travel; the clause may coordinate with the conditional verb or describe a state.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r1.anchor: ففيه استعارة تبعية حيث شبه تمكنهم في السفر بتمكن الراكب من مركوبه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya reads kutuban, while al-Hasan and Ibn Abbas read kitaban.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو العالية كتبا والحسن وابن عباس كتابا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r3.claim: Rahn can mean the means of security, something to be taken, or the prescribed pledge; rahn began as a verbal noun and then named the pledged object.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r3.anchor: وهو في الأصل مصدر ثم أطلق على المرهون من باب إطلاق المصدر على اسم المفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r4.claim: The travel and lack of a scribe indicate when a pledge substitutes for documentary security, not conditions on its validity; the Prophet pledged his armor to a Jew in Medina for thirty measures of barley.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r4.anchor: بل لإقامة التوثق بالارتهان مقام التوثق بالكتبة في السفر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r5.claim: Mujahid takes the verse literally and permits pledges only during travel.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r5.anchor: وأخذ مجاهد بظاهر الآية فذهب إلى أن الرهن لا يجوز إلا في السفر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r6.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says a pledge during travel is lawful only when no scribe is available.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r6.anchor: وكذا الضحاك فذهب إلى أنه لا يجوز في السفر إلا عند فقد الكاتب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r7.claim: The majority require the pledge to be physically delivered to complete it.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r7.anchor: والجمهور على وجوب القبض في تمام الرهن

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r8.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r8.claim: Malik holds that offer and acceptance complete the pledge and make delivery binding; if the pledge returns absolutely to the debtor’s hand, it leaves the pledge and shares among creditors.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r8.anchor: وذهب مالك إلى أنه يتم بالإيجاب والقبول ويلزم الرهن بالعقد تسليمه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r9.speaker: أبو علي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r9.claim: Abu Ali’s verse uses rahin for bread and meat as things still held or remaining, illustrating the pledge’s implication of continuity.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r9.anchor: أنشد أبو على : فالخبز وللحم لهن راهن

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r10.claim: The passive adjective maqbudah suggests that a proxy’s possession suffices; the mortgagee need not personally take possession.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r10.anchor: وفي التعبير بمقبوضة دون تقبضونها إياءا إلى الاكتفاء بقبض الوكيل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r11.claim: Other readings have rahun, with a rounded plural pattern, or rahn with a light, vowelless ha.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r11.anchor: وقرئ فرهن كسقف وهو جمع رهن أيضا وقرئ بسكون الهاء تخفيفا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r12.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r12.claim: Ubayy’s reading makes the debtor’s trustworthiness passive: people have entrusted him and described him as faithful and reliable.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r12.anchor: وقرأ أبي فإن أو من أي أمنه الناس ووصفوا المديون بالأمانة والوفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r13.claim: If some trust others, the debt is left unsecured by writing, witnesses, or pledge, whether they are traveling or resident.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r13.anchor: بعض الدائنين بعض المديونين بحسن ظنه سفرا أو حضرا فلم يتوثق بالكتابة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r14.claim: The person entrusted is the debtor, named by that description to identify him and encourage repayment; amānah denotes the debt owed.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r14.anchor: وهو المديون وعبر عنه بذلك العنوان لتعينه طريقا للإعلام ولحمله على الأداء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r15.claim: The debt is called a trust because the creditor has left it unsecured, relying on the debtor to repay; the possessive pronoun can refer to creditor or debtor.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r15.anchor: وإنما سمى أمانة وهو مضمون لائمانه عليه بترك الإرتهان به

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r16.speaker: عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r16.claim: Asim’s assimilated reading of the hamza-derived form is criticized by some as an error, but al-Alusi cites its attestation in Arabic and the Kufan grammatical position permitting it.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r16.anchor: وعن عاصم أنه قرأ الذتمن بإدغام الياء في التاء وقيل هو خطأ

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r17.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r17.claim: Al-Saghani cites Aisha’s fluent speech as an Arabic parallel for assimilation, recorded in al-Bukhari as the Prophet directing her to wear a waist wrapper.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r17.anchor: وورد مثله فى كلام أم المؤمنين عائشة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r18.claim: The command to fear God at repayment, as at the original acknowledgment, stresses human rights and guards against betrayal and corruption.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p62/r18.anchor: وقد أمر سبحانه بالتقوى عند الوفاء حسبما أمر بها عند الإقرار تعظيما لحقوق العباد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r1.claim: Do not conceal testimony by refusing to give it when summoned; the address is to believing witnesses, as transmitted from early authorities.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r1.anchor: أي لا تخفوها بالامتناع عن أدائها إذا دعيتم إليها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and others are cited for reading the command as addressed to witnesses.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r2.anchor: وهو خطاب للشهود المؤمنين كما روي عن سعيد بن جبير وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r3.claim: An alternative address to debtors, meaning they should acknowledge debt or avoid defeating witnesses in court, conflicts with the apparent wording and early transmitted interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r3.anchor: خلاف الظاهر المأثور عن السلف الصالح

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r4.claim: A variant reads the verb for concealing in the third-person plural.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r5.claim: The pronoun in innahu most naturally returns to whoever conceals testimony; some make it a pronoun of the matter, though a following participial phrase is not a sentence for Basran and Kufan grammarians.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r5.anchor: الضمير فى أنه راجع إلى ( من ) وهو الظاهر وقيل : إنه ضمير الشأن

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r6.claim: Grammarians parse āthim as predicate with qalb as its subject, as predicate before a delayed subject, or with qalb in apposition; al-Farra and al-Akhfash also allow qalb as the subject of āthim, a construction most grammarians reject.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r6.anchor: وهذا جائز عند الفراء من الكوفيين والأخفش من البصريين وجمهور النحاة لا يجوز

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r7.claim: Attributing the sin to the heart is concise because concealment is an inward act; naming the chief organ intensifies the warning and shows the enormity of the sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r7.anchor: ولأن الإثم وإن كان منسوبا إلى جملة الشخص لكنه اعتبر الإسناد إلى هذا الجزء المخصوص

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r8.claim: Al-Alusi dismisses additional explanations that the attribution alludes to a black mark from sin or to the heart’s effect on the whole body.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r8.anchor: والكل ليس بشئ كما لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r9.claim: A variant puts qalb in the accusative by analogy with an object; Abu Hayyan permits it as partitive apposition, while some call it specification and Abu al-Baqa rejects that.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r9.anchor: وقرئ قلبه بالنصب على التشبيه بالمفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r10.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r10.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads āthama qalbahu, making the heart sinful.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبى عبلة ( آثم قلبه ) أى جعله آثما

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r11.claim: God knows whether people conceal testimony or deliver it properly and will repay them accordingly.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63/r11.anchor: والله بما تعملون من كتمان الشهادة وأدائها على وجهها وغير ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p63#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63#2/r1.claim: God repays each person according to the conduct at issue: good is repaid with good and evil with evil.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p63#2/r1.anchor: فيجازيكم بذلك إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.claim: They read furuhun with ḍamma on rāʾ and hāʾ; other readers have rihān, a plural of rahn, and some grammarians analyze it as a plural of rihān.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو فرهن بضم الهاء والراء، وقرأ الباقون فرهان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.claim: Abu ʿAmr says he chose furuhun to distinguish the pledge word from rihān, horse racing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو وإنما قرأنا فرهن ليكون فرقا بينهما وبين رهان الخيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.claim: Ikrima reads ruhun with ḍamma on rāʾ and a quiescent hāʾ; light and geminated forms are both Arabic variants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة فرهن بضم الراء وسكون الهاء، والتخفيف والتثقيل في الرهن لغتان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.claim: When traveling without writing equipment, take collateral to secure the debt. Jurists agree a pledge is effective only after possession; once delivered, the pledger cannot reclaim it while any debt remains.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.anchor: فارتهنوا ممن تداينونه رهونا لتكون وثيقة لكم بأموالكم، واتفقوا على أن الرهن لا يتم إلا بالقبض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.claim: A pledge is valid at home even if a scribe is available.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.anchor: ويجوز في الحضر الرهن مع وجود الكاتب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.claim: Mujahid limits pledging to travel when no scribe is available, following the verse's apparent condition; others say travel describes the usual situation, not a legal condition.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لا يجوز الرهن إلا في السفر عند عدم الكاتب لظاهر الآية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.claim: The Prophet's pledge of his armor to the Jewish creditor Abu al-Shahm shows that a pledge is valid outside travel and when a scribe is available.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.anchor: والدليل عليه ما روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رهن درعه عند أبي الشحم اليهودي ولم يكن ذلك في السفر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r8.claim: In Ubayy's reading, if the debtor is trusted, the creditor leaves the debt uncollateralized because of his good opinion of him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p352#2/r8.anchor: وفي حرف أبي "فإن ائتمن" يعني فإن كان الذي عليه الحق أمينا عند صاحب الحق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r1.claim: The trusted debtor must repay what was entrusted and fear God in fulfilling the debt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r1.anchor: {فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته} أي فليقضه على الأمانة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r2.claim: The passage returns to witnesses: they must not conceal testimony when called to give it; concealing it incurs a grave threat, and sinful heart means a corrupted heart, perhaps transformed by punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r2.anchor: ثم رجع إلى خطاب الشهود وقال: {ولا تكتموا الشهادة}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r3.claim: God knows whether testimony is disclosed or withheld.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p353/r3.anchor: والله بما تعملون} بيان الشهادة وكتمانها {عليم}

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r1.claim: Without a scribe while traveling, take a pledge as security; the clause may say that a pledge is security, pledges are due, or a pledge should be taken.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r1.anchor: فالذي يستوثق به رهان، أو فعليكم رهان، أو فليؤخذ رهان.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r2.claim: Travel does not condition the validity of a pledge, contrary to Mujahid and Dahhak: the Prophet pledged his armor in Medina to a Jew for twenty measures of barley.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r2.anchor: وليس هذا التعليق لاشتراط السفر في الارتهان كما ظنه مجاهد والضحاك رحمهما الله تعالى لأنه عليه السلام رهن درعه في المدينة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r3.claim: The travel clause places pledging where writing is likely unavailable; most require possession for a pledge, unlike Malik.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r3.anchor: بل لإقامة التوثق للإرتهان مقام التوثق بالكتابة في السفر الذي هو مظنة إعوازها. والجمهور على اعتبار القبض فيه غير مالك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read ruhun, a plural of rahn meaning pledged; a sukun reading lightens the vowel.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو «فرهن» كسقف وكلاهما جمع رهن بمعنى مرهون:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r5.claim: If creditors trust debtors, they need no pledge; the entrusted person must repay, the debt called a trust because the creditor left it unsecured.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r5.anchor: أي دينه سماه أمانة لائتمانه عليه بترك الارتهان به.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r6.claim: The reading itamin changes hamza into yāʾ; ataman with assimilation is erroneous because the letter from hamza retains hamza's status.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r6.anchor: وقرىء «الذي ايتمن» بقلب الهمزة ياء، و «الذي أتمن» بإدغام الياء في التاء وهو خطأ

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r7.claim: The debtor must fear God against betrayal or denial; the phrasing contains several intensifiers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r7.anchor: في الخيانة وإنكار الحق وفيه مبالغات.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r8.claim: The prohibition on concealing testimony addresses witnesses, or debtors testifying against themselves.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r8.anchor: أيها الشهود، أو المدينون والشهادة شهادتهم على أنفسهم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r9.claim: The heart may itself sin or be sinful; the attribution highlights the concealer's act, the heart's primacy, or the idea that sin permeates the self.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r9.anchor: أي يأثم قلبه أو قلبه يأثم. والجملة خبر إن وإسناد الإثم إلى القلب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r10.claim: The construction resembles saying the eye and ear commit adultery; qalbuhu also has an accusative reading, and God's knowledge is a threat.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:283/r10.anchor: ونظيره: العين زانية والأذن زانية. أو للمبالغة فإنه رئيس الأعضاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r1.claim: Travelers lacking a scribe may substitute a pledge for written documentation; the pledge is valid only when actually held by the creditor.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r1.anchor: أي فيغنيكم عن الكتب رهن يكون بدلا عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r2.claim: The readings رهان and رهن are both plurals of rهن; a pledge secures a debt with something of corresponding value.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r2.anchor: وهو التوثقة بالشيء مما يعادله بوجه ما

BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r3.claim: If the parties trust each other, no writing or pledge is needed; trust may be mutual in either direction, and the entrusted debtor must repay on time.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r3.anchor: ولما كان الائتمان تارة يكون من الدائن وتارة يكون من الراهن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r4.claim: The debt is called a trust because the lender waived security out of goodwill and good opinion; the debtor must repay faithfully and fear God as his Lord.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r4.anchor: وهو الدين الذي ترك المؤتمن التوثق به من المدين إحسانا إليه وحسن ظن به

BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r5.claim: Witnesses must not conceal testimony, whether or not the claimant already knows it; greed, fear, or hope can otherwise silence them and create conflict.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r5.anchor: أي سواء كان صاحب الحق يعلمها أو لا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r6.claim: Calling the concealing witness sinful in heart identifies the heart as the body's foundation; a corrupted heart corrupts the whole body.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p550/r6.anchor: ومن أثم قلبه فسد , ومن فسد قلبه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p551/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p551/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p551/r1.claim: God's encompassing knowledge includes every deed, however slight, and even deeds of the heart alone; this knowledge threatens any witness who evades testimony.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p551/r1.anchor: أي كله وإن دق سواء كان فعل القلب وحده أو لا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p551/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p551/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p551/r2.claim: Al-Harali says the passage closes the discussion of relations between God and people and between people themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p551/r2.anchor: فأنهى أمر ما بين الحق والخلق ممثولا وأمر ما بين الخلق والخلق مثلا

DURR-FULL:v2p118/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p118/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p118/r1.claim: Concealing testimony is a grave sin because God says the concealer's heart is sinful.
DURR-FULL:v2p118/r1.anchor:
ومن الكبائر كتمان الشهادة
قال: لأن الله تعالى يقول (ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه

DURR-FULL:v2p124/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r1.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says knowledge sustains Islam and faith, and one who learns and acts is taught by God what he did not know.
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r1.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم العلم حياة الإسلام وعماد الإيمان

DURR-FULL:v2p124/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reads 'if you do not find a writing instrument'; a scribe may exist while pen, ink, or paper is unavailable, and 'kitāb' encompasses them all; Ubayy read likewise.
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قرأ (ولم تجدوا كتابا) وقال: قد يوجد الكاتب ولا يوجد القلم ولا الدواة ولا الصحيفة

DURR-FULL:v2p124/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya reads 'if you do not find writing materials,' explaining that a scribe may exist without ink or paper.
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية أنه كان يقرأ (فإن لم تجدوا كتابا) قال: يوجد الكاتب ولا توجد الدواة ولا الصحيفة

DURR-FULL:v2p124/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak also reads the phrase as 'if you do not find writing materials.'
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r5.anchor:
ابن الأنباري عن الضحاك
مثله
وأخرج أبو عبيد وعبد بن

DURR-FULL:v2p124/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r6.claim: ʿIkrima reads 'if you do not find writing materials.'
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة أنه قرأها (فإن لم تجدوا كتابا

DURR-FULL:v2p124/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r7.claim: Mujahid reads 'if you do not find ink' and glosses the word as ink.
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قرأها (فإن لم تجدوا كتابا) قال: مدادا

DURR-FULL:v2p124/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says scribes were widespread among Arabs, but they often lacked paper, pen, and ink.
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها (فإن لم تجدوا كتابا) وقال: الكتاب كثير لم يكن حواء من العرب

DURR-FULL:v2p124/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas also read the phrase with a damma on kāf and a doubled tāʾ.
DURR-FULL:v2p124/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ (ولم تجدوا كتابا) بضم الكاف وتشديد التاء

DURR-FULL:v2p125/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r1.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says the Prophet taught him the reading 'a pledged security' without the alif.
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r1.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فرهن مقبوضة) بغير ألف

DURR-FULL:v2p125/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r2.speaker: حميد الأعرج وإبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r2.claim: Humayd al-Aʿraj and Ibrahim read the phrase as 'pledges' without an alif.
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r2.anchor: عن حميد الأعرج وإبراهيم أنهما قرآ (فرهن مقبوضة

DURR-FULL:v2p125/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r3.speaker: الحسن وأبو الرجاء
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu al-Rajaʾ read it with the word for pledges in the plural, with an alif.
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r3.anchor: عن الحسن وأبي الرجاء أنهما قرآ {فرهان مقبوضة

DURR-FULL:v2p125/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says a traveler unable to find a scribe for a deferred sale may take a pledge, but may not do so if a scribe is available.
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r4.anchor:
عن الضحاك في قوله {وإن كنتم على سفر} الآية
قال: من كان على سفر فبايع بيعا إلى أجل فلم يجد كاتبا

DURR-FULL:v2p125/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r5.claim: Mujahid says pledges are permitted only during travel.
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا فرهان مقبوضة} قال: لا يكون الرهان إلا في السفر

DURR-FULL:v2p125/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r6.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r6.claim: The Prophet bought food on credit from a Jewish seller and pledged his iron armor.
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r6.anchor: عن عائشة قالت اشترى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم طعاما من يهودي بنسيئة ورهنه درعا له من حديد

DURR-FULL:v2p125/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r7.claim: If a traveler cannot document a debt, the creditor may take a pledge; if the debtor is trusted, the creditor may rely on that trust, and the debtor must repay and fear God.
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا} يعني لم تقدروا على كتابة الدين في السفر

DURR-FULL:v2p125/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r8.claim: A pledge must be physically received by the creditor.
DURR-FULL:v2p125/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: لا يكون الرهن إلا مقبوضا يقبضه الذي له المال

DURR-FULL:v2p126/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p126/r2.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v2p126/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says if the parties trust one another, writing and witnessing may be omitted.
DURR-FULL:v2p126/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: لا بأس إذا أمنته أن لا تكتب ولا تشهد لقوله {فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا

DURR-FULL:v2p126/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p126/r3.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v2p126/r3.claim: No one may conceal testimony, even testimony against oneself, one's parents, or close relatives.
DURR-FULL:v2p126/r3.anchor: عن الربيع {ولا تكتموا الشهادة} قال: لا يحل لأحد أن يكتم شهادة هي عنده وإن كانت على نفسه

DURR-FULL:v2p126/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p126/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p126/r4.claim: A sinful heart is a wicked heart.
DURR-FULL:v2p126/r4.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {آثم قلبه} قال: فاجر قلبه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r1.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r1.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī defines guardianship as preservation and rectification, noting that the root originally referred to protecting livestock by feeding it or warding off predators.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r1.anchor: وجاء في (روح المعاني) تفسير (راعون) : "قائمون بحفظها وإصلاحها.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r2.claim: The author says riyāʿa is broader than mere preservation: it includes care, correction, stewardship, and monitoring, all needed to discharge a trust.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r2.anchor: فالرعي ليس مجرد الحفظ؛ بل هو الحِفْظُ والإصلاح والعناية بالأمر وتولي شأنه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r3.claim: A trusted guardian must attend to dependents’ needs, a ruler must oversee subjects, and one entrusted with crops, livestock, or religious obligations must actively discharge the charge and seek what pleases God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r3.anchor: فمن ائتمن عندك أهله وصغاره، فلا بد من أن تتفقد أمورهم وتنظر في أحوالهم وحاجاتهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r4.claim: Unlike chastity, which remains with the person, trusts may be remote or hidden from view and exposed to thieves, so the trustee must inspect and tend them like a shepherd; riyāʿa is the apt term.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r4.anchor: فهي تحتاج إلى تفقد ورعاية كما يحتاج الحيوان إلى حفظه من الذئاب والوحوش الضارية.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r5.claim: The nominal form raaʿūn, rather than the verb yarʿawn, signals that this guardianship must remain constant and never lapse.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p149/r5.anchor: لم يقل: (يرعون) ذلك ليدلَّ على لزوم ثبات الرعي ودوامه وعدم الإخلال به البتة.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r1.claim: The author says responsible transmission requires fulfilling its trust by checking the accuracy of what is reported.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r1.anchor: من تأدية أمانته، وتحري الصحة في روايته

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r2.claim: The introduction presents Ibn Jinni as critically testing inherited material, sometimes gently and sometimes forcefully, while pursuing truth fairly and independently.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r2.anchor: لم يكن ابن جني يتقبل كل ما ينقله أو يأخذه على ما خيلت؛ ولكنه كان ينظر فيه وينقده

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r5.claim: Ibn Jinni openly transmits the evidence, principles, and debated conclusions he received from his teacher Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, then adds his own comment.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r5.anchor: ونقل عن شيخه أبي علي الفارسي، فروى مما أنشده إياه من شواهد، وما أخذه عنه من أصول

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r1.claim: The author sets out to discuss readings outside the seven canonical readers, asking God for aid.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r1.anchor: بادئ بكتاب أذكر فيه أحوال ما شذ عن السبعة

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r2.claim: He distinguishes plain anomalous readings, which need no discussion, from obscure readings that strain ordinary grammatical analysis and form the book’s focus.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r2.anchor: وضرب ثان وهو هذا الذي نحن على سمته؛ أعني: ما شذ عن السبعة، وغمض عن ظاهر الصنعة

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r3.claim: For the readings he treats, he combines his own transmissions with accounts verified from others and promises fidelity and accuracy.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r3.anchor: ونحن نورد ذلك على ما رويناه، ثم على ما صح عندنا من طريق رواية غيرنا له

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r4.claim: He directs readers to Ibn Mujāhid’s book because it is specifically devoted to anomalous readings and is more trustworthy than many reports from less reliable authorities.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r4.anchor: ننحي4 فيه على كتاب أبي بكر أحمد بن موسى بن مجاهد -رحمه الله- الذي وضعه لذكر الشواذ

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r5.claim: Abū Ḥātim’s collection is more comprehensive than Qutrub’s because it focuses on readings, while Qutrub gives extensive explanation and supporting evidence.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r5.anchor: غير أن كتاب أبي حاتم أجمع من كتاب قطرب لذلك؛ من حيث كان مقصورا على ذكر القراءات

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r6.speaker: محمد بن صالح المصري
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ reports that Qutrub read from al-Naḥl to the end of the Qurʾān, and that ʿAlī ibn Qutrub read from al-Baqara through al-Naḥl from his father in Egypt in 249 AH.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p34/r6.anchor: قال: حدثني محمد بن صالح المصري2 وراق على بن قطرب، قال: قرأت على أبي محمد بن المستنير قطرب

NASHR:v1p342#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p342#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p342#2/r1.claim: Although early authorities do not explicitly identify this altered-hamza case, al-Jazari says al-Shatibi’s wording includes it and that this is sound in performance and should be adopted; he still allows a rule-based disagreement.
NASHR:v1p342#2/r1.anchor: نعم عبارة الشاطبي صريحة بدخوله ; ولذلك مثل به شراح كلامه، وهو الذي صح أداء، وبه يؤخذ

NASHR:v1p342#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p342#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p342#2/r2.claim: At word onset after the article’s lām, ignoring its incidental vowel permits both lengths, while treating it as operative permits only shortening; Makkī says Warsh does not lengthen الأولى.
NASHR:v1p342#2/r2.anchor: أما حالة الابتداء إذا وقع بعد لام التعريف فإن لم يعتد بالعارض، فالوجهان في نحو (الآخرة)

NASHR:v1p342#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p342#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p342#2/r3.claim: For a madd letter after hamzat al-wasl at onset, al-Dani, Abu Mashar, and al-Shatibi explicitly exclude lengthening, while Ibn Sufyan, Ibn Shurayh, and Makkī leave it out; al-Tabsira calls both acceptable and shortening more analogical.
NASHR:v1p342#2/r3.anchor: وأما الأصل المطرد الذي فيه الخلاف فهو حرف المد إذا وقع بعد همزة الوصل حالة الابتداء نحو (ايت بقرآن. ايتوني اوتمن ايذن لي)

NASHR:v1p342#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p342#2/r4.speaker: ابن سفيان وابن شريح ومكي
NASHR:v1p342#2/r4.claim: Ibn Sufyan, Ibn Shurayh, and Makkī omit the two length options for a madd letter after initial hamzat al-wasl; al-Tabsira says both are good but shortening is more analogical.
NASHR:v1p342#2/r4.anchor: وتركه ابن سفيان وابن شريح ومكي، وقال في " التبصرة ": وكلا الوجهين حسن، وترك المد أقيس

NASHR:v1p351/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p351/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p351/r1.claim: Madd causes rank from strongest to weakest: pronounced causes outrank semantic ones; among pronounced causes, a still letter outranks connected hamza, then separated hamza, while incidental stillness is weakest.
NASHR:v1p351/r1.anchor: لإجماعهم عليه، وكان الساكن أقوى من الهمز ; لأن المد فيه يقوم مقام الحركة

NASHR:v1p351/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p351/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p351/r2.claim: A still letter needs madd to be articulated fully, so readers agree on one measure; connected outranks separated because consensus requires the former, while they differ on the latter.
NASHR:v1p351/r2.anchor: فلا يتمكن من النطق بالساكن بحقه إلا بالمد ; ولذلك اتفق الجمهور على مده قدرا واحدا

NASHR:v1p351/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p351/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p351/r3.claim: Madd is mandatory by consensus when condition and cause are both necessary and strong, forbidden when a required element is absent or both are weak, and otherwise disputed; when causes combine, the stronger governs.
NASHR:v1p351/r3.anchor: فمتى اجتمع الشرط والسبب مع اللزوم والقوة لزم المد ووجب إجماعا، ومتى تخلف أحدهما

NASHR:v1p351/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p351/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p351/r4.claim: No madd is allowed in خلوا إلى or ابني آدم because condition and separated cause are weak; Warsh via al-Azraq may lengthen سوءة and هيئة because the cause is connected.
NASHR:v1p351/r4.anchor: لا يجوز مد نحو (خلوا إلى، وابني آدم) كما تقدم، وذلك لضعف الشرط باختلاف حركة ما قبله والسبب بالانفصال

NASHR:v1p351/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p351/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p351/r5.claim: The strong stillness cause permits madd in عين and هذين in both states, and in الموت and الليل at pause.
NASHR:v1p351/r5.anchor: ويجوز مد نحو (سوءة، وهيئة) لورش من طريق الأزرق كما تقدم؛ لقوة السبب بالاتصال

NASHR:v1p472/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p472/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p472/r1.claim: For الذي اؤتمن and related forms, al-Jazari rejects verification of the hamza and extra madd over the substituted letter; only substitution with shortening and fatḥ is valid.
NASHR:v1p472/r1.anchor: ولا يصح من كلها سوى وجه واحد، وهو البدل مع القصر والفتح

NASHR:v1p472/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p472/r2.speaker: أبو شامة
NASHR:v1p472/r2.claim: Abu Shama proposes either restoring the original madd letter after hamza substitution or deleting it because a still letter follows; he links this to possible imala in إلى الهدى ايتنا.
NASHR:v1p472/r2.anchor: فإذا أبدل هذا الهمز حرف مد، وكان قبله من جنسه، وكان يحذف لأجل سكون الهمزة

NASHR:v1p472/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p472/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p472/r3.claim: Al-Jazari rejects Abu Shama’s analogy: the earlier madd letter was already deleted to resolve two still letters, so it cannot return because of pause substitution; only the shortened, open substitution remains.
NASHR:v1p472/r3.anchor: فلا يجوز رده لعروض الوقف بالبدل كما لا يجوز لعروض النقل

NASHR:v1p381/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p381/r1.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v1p381/r1.claim: The alif insertion between the two hamzas in أئمة was also transmitted from Nafi and Abu Amr, besides Abu Jaafar.
NASHR:v1p381/r1.anchor: لم ينفرد أبو جعفر بإدخال الألف بين الهمزة المحققة والمسهلة في (أئمة) بل ورد ذلك عن نافع وأبي عمرو

NASHR:v1p381/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p381/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p381/r2.claim: Readers who insert alif do so when the second hamza is fully realized or softened between two sounds; they do not insert it when that hamza is changed to pure yāʾ.
NASHR:v1p381/r2.anchor: فكل من فصل بالألف بينهما من المحققين إنما يفصل بها في حال تسهيلها بين بين، ولا يجوز الفصل بها في حال إبدالها الياء المحضة

NASHR:v1p381/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p381/r3.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p381/r3.claim: Al-Dani says the imams who use separation do not read a pure kasra-yāʾ, since their inserted alif presupposes a realized hamza; pure yāʾ is the grammarians’ approach.
NASHR:v1p381/r3.anchor: قال الداني بعد ذكر من يسهلها بين بين: ولا تكون ياء محضة الكسرة في مذهبهم

NASHR:v1p381/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p381/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p381/r4.claim: All readers obligatorily replace a non-interrogative still hamza after a moving hamza with a madd letter matching the preceding vowel: alif after fatha, waw after damma, and yāʾ after kasra.
NASHR:v1p381/r4.anchor: فإن الهمزة الثانية منهما تبدل في ذلك كله حرف مد من جنس ما قبلها، فتبدل ألفا بعد المفتوحة، وواوا بعد المضمومة

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r3.claim: The apparent reading is الكاتب in the singular, as in the codex.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r3.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة ولم تجدوا كاتبا على الواحد

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو العالية
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Abū al-ʿĀliya read كتابا, explaining that one might find a writer but lack writing materials.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبي العالية (كتابا) قالوا: ربما يجد الكاتب ولا يجد آلات الكتابة،

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r5.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reads كتابا as a plural meaning writers.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r5.anchor: وعن الضحاك كتابا على جمع الكاتب

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read فرهن with ḍamma on rāʾ and hāʾ.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: فرهن بضم الراء والهاء

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r7.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read رهان.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: فرهان

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r8.speaker: عكرمة
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r8.claim: ʿIkrima is reported to read فرهن.

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r9.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r9.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ parse رُهُن as a plural of رهان, itself the plural of رهن, a plural-of-a-plural pattern.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r9.anchor: فأما الرهن بضم الراء وجزم الهاء فجمع رهان، وهو جمع الجمع رهن ورهان ورهن، نحو: تمر وتمار وتمر، عن الكسائي والفراء،

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r10.speaker: أبو عبيد
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r10.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says رهن may be a singular whose plural is formed like سقف and سقف.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r10.anchor: وقيل: واحده رهن، نحو: سقف وسقف، عن أبي عبيد

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r11.claim: Some grammarians say these are the only nouns with the two cited vocalized patterns; others add the palm heart, قلب النخلة.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r11.anchor: وقيل: لا يعرف في الأسماء فعل وفعل غير هذين، وزاد بعضهم: قلب النخلة وقلب

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r12.claim: Rihān is the regular plural of rهن, like ḥibāl from ḥabl and biġāl from baġl.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r12.anchor: فأما رهان جمع رهن فعلى القياس نحو حبل وحبال وبغل وبغال

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r13.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r13.claim: Abū ʿAmr prefers فرهن because that form is common in horse-betting and matches the codex.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r13.anchor: واختار أبو عمرو فرهن لغلبة الرهان في الخيل، ولموافقة المصحف،

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r14.claim: Those preferring رهان cite its regularity as a plural pattern across kinds.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r14.anchor: ومن اختار الرهان فلاطراده في باب الجمع، وكل جنس.

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r15.claim: The apparent reading uses the second-person tāʾ.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r15.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة ولا تكتموا بالتاء وعن السلمي بالياء

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r16.speaker: السلمي
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r16.claim: Al-Sulamī is reported to read the verb with third-person yāʾ.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r16.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة ولا تكتموا بالتاء وعن السلمي بالياء

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r17.claim: Rahn means holding something as security; rahantu is more eloquent than arhantu, and anything held for another is a pledge or collateral.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r17.anchor: الرهن: مصدر رهنت الشيء أرهنه رهنا، وأرهنت أيضا، والأول أفصح، والرهن: حبس الشيء عليه،

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r18.claim: With emphatic ḍād, qabḍ is grasping an object in the palm; with un-emphatic ṣād, qabṣ is gripping it with the fingertips.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r18.anchor: والقبض - بالضاد معجمة -: قبض الشيء ملء الكف، وبالصاد - غير معجمة -: القبض بأطراف الأصابع.

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r19.claim: Iʾtumana is the eighth-form verb derived from amāna, trust.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r19.anchor: وأتمن افتعل من الأمانة. والكتمان: ضد الإظهار.

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r20.claim: Kitmān, concealment, is the opposite of disclosure.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r20.anchor: وأتمن افتعل من الأمانة. والكتمان: ضد الإظهار.

JISHUMI:v2p1081/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r21.claim: Rahn is nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject such as الوثيقة; it may also follow فعليه or be accusative under an implied instruction to take a pledge.
JISHUMI:v2p1081/r21.anchor: رفع رهن لأنه خبر ابتداء محذوف، وتقديره: فالوثيقة رهن، ويجوز فعليه رهن، ويجوز فرهنا بالنصب في العربية،

JISHUMI:v2p1082/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r1.claim: After describing documentation by witnesses, the passage turns to collateral as documentation when a writer and witnesses are unavailable while traveling.
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r1.anchor: لما تقدم حكم الوثيقة بالإشهاد أتبعه ذكر الوثيقة بالرهن عند عدم الإشهاد

JISHUMI:v2p1082/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r2.claim: A pledge is security taken from a debtor to protect the creditor's property.
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r2.anchor: فرهان أي فالوثيقة رهن، وهو أن يأخذ ممن داينه رهنا وثيقة بماله مقبوضة

JISHUMI:v2p1082/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r3.claim: A pledge is not valid unless possessed by the pledgee, by consensus and textual proof, because security is not complete until possession.
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r3.anchor: فإن الرهن لا يصح إلا مقبوضا بالإجماع والنص؛ لأن الوثيقة لا تتم إلا بالقبض،

JISHUMI:v2p1082/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r4.claim: The creditor trusts the debtor and therefore dispenses with writing, witnesses, and collateral.
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r4.anchor: يعني الذي له الحق يأتمن من عليه فلا يكتب ولا يشهد ولا يرتهن

JISHUMI:v2p1082/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r5.claim: The preferred address is to the debtor: the trusted party must repay the debt.
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r5.anchor: فليؤد خطاب للمديون يعني فليؤد المؤتمن أمانته يعني حقه

JISHUMI:v2p1082/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r6.claim: Alternatively, the command addresses the pledgee, who must return the collateral after the debt is paid because it is a trust in his hands; the debtor reading is preferred.
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r6.anchor: وقيل: خطاب للمرتهن بأن يؤدي الرهن عند استيفاء المال، فإنه أمانة في يده، والأول الوجه

JISHUMI:v2p1082/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r7.claim: To fear God here means not to violate His command.
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r7.anchor: وليتق الله ربه يعني مخالفة أمره

JISHUMI:v2p1082/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r8.claim: The address shifts to witnesses, who may have witnessed the pledge or attended the contract without being formally asked to testify; they are still charged to provide evidence.
JISHUMI:v2p1082/r8.anchor: عاد الخطاب إلى الشهود قيل: لأنه قد يكون شاهدا على الرهن، وقيل: لأنه قد يحضر العقد وإن لم يستشهد، فكلف أن يقيم البينة

BURHAN:v4p220/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p220/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p220/r6.claim: For the remaining examples, the apparent conditional sense is contextually implausible, but an incidental factor can still license departure from the surface reading.
BURHAN:v4p220/r6.anchor: واما البواقي فظاهر الشرط ممتنع فيه بدليل التعجب المذكور لكنه لا يمنع مخالفة الظاهر لعارض

BURHAN:v4p220/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p220/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p220/r7.claim: The travel-and-collateral clause is among the Qur'anic conditional constructions whose condition is discussed as not necessarily intended literally.
BURHAN:v4p220/r7.anchor: ﴿ وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا فرهان مقبوضة ﴾

BURHAN:v4p220/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p220/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p220/r8.claim: The separate open-hamza particle an is a verbal-noun particle governing a subjunctive imperfect; its clause can serve as subject, agent, object, or genitive complement.
BURHAN:v4p220/r8.anchor: حرفا مصدريا ناصبا للفعل المضارع وتقع معه في موقع المبتدأ والفاعل والمفعول والمضاف إليه

BURHAN:v1p410/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p410/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p410/r1.claim: The written feminine ending has two aspects: as a name or quality its ta is closed; when it signifies an act or visible effect, it is extended.
BURHAN:v1p410/r1.anchor: أحدهما من حيث هى أسماء وصفات وهذا تقبض منه التاء والثانى من حيث أن يكون مقتضاها فعلا وأثرا ظاهرا فى الوجود فهذا تمد فيه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r1.claim: Difficult expression is condemned when it entangles thought, obstructs the route to meaning, and leaves the reader unsure how to reach it.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r1.anchor: يعثر فكرك في متصرفه ويشيك طريقك إلى المعنى ويوعر مذهبك نحوه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r2.claim: Clear expression opens and prepares a straight path for thought; even where the path bends, it supplies markers that make progress confident.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r2.anchor: وأما الملخص فيفتح لفكرتك الطريق المستوى ويمهده وإن كان فيه تعاطف أقام عليه المنار

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r3.claim: An aphorism locates delight and ease of heart in four things: clear proof, loved companions, confidence in provision, and seeing the goal.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r3.anchor: فقد قيل قرة العين وسعة الصدر وروح القلب وطيب النفس من أربعة أمور الاستبانة للحجة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r4.speaker: الجاحظ
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r4.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ contrasts animal pleasures with the joy of intellectual victory and discovering knowledge after sustained inquiry.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r4.anchor: وقال الجاحظ في أثناء فصل يذكر فيه ما في الفكر والنظر من الفضيلة وأين تقع لذة البهيمة بالعلوفة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r5.speaker: الجاحظ
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r5.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ likens intellectual competition to races and target practice: minds contend through reflection, reasoning, analogy, and inference.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r5.anchor: وقال الجاحظ في أثناء فصل يذكر فيه ما في الفكر والنظر من الفضيلة وأين تقع لذة البهيمة بالعلوفة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r6.claim: The finest craft joins disparate things by subtle affinities; the more unlike its parts are yet the more fully harmonized, the more admirable the result.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p125/r6.anchor: كلما كانت أجزاؤها أشد اختلافا في الشكل والهيئة ثم كان التلاؤم بينها مع ذلك أتم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r1.claim: The poem makes two hands alike in form while contrasting their numbers and place values, joining visual agreement to quantitative difference.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r1.anchor: أراك شكلا واحدا في اليدين مع اختلاف العددين ومع اختلاف المرتبتين في العدد أيضا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r2.speaker: المرزباني
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r2.claim: Al-Marzubānī credits al-Khalīl with inventing the comparison of the two contracted hands to differently scaled numerical forms.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r2.anchor: قال المرزبانى وهذا مما أبدع فيه الخليل لأنه وصف انقباض اليدين

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r3.claim: Another rhetorical kind depicts an action as producing its opposite, such as doing good while intending harm or benefiting while seeking injury.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r3.anchor: الجنس الذي يراد فيه كون الشىء من الأفعال سببا لضده كقولنا أحسن من حيث قصد الإساءة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r4.claim: The poet recasts blameworthy withholding as generosity and a cause of gratitude, making a censured act seem praiseworthy through its consequence.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r4.anchor: في نفس الإساءة الإحسان وفي البخل الجود وفي المنع العطاء وفي موجب الذم موجب الحمد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r5.claim: The reversal succeeds when it preserves both a pleasing agreement and a clear opposition, then states the hidden point precisely and elegantly.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r5.anchor: بما يكون فيه من الوفاق الحسن مع الخلاف البين على حذق شاعرة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r6.speaker: أبو العتاهية
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r6.claim: Jurjānī presents Abū al-ʿAtāhiya’s verses as an example in which a miser’s withholding is turned into a benefit for the recipient.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p133/r6.anchor: قول أبي العتاهية ( جزى البخيل على صالحة عنى لخفته على ظهرى )
